attorneys.name: John McCormick
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Norfolk, VA
attorneys.bio:
John is passionate about entrepreneurship and business development. He has personally launched multiple new ventures and ideas. Like many entrepreneurs, some ventures have succeeded while others have failed. A true believer in "failing forward", John looks for new opportunities in every situation. This mentality allows John to connect with entrepreneurs and business owners in a meaningful way to help them navigate difficulties and grow their success.

Outside of his practice of law, John serves as Chairman of the Board for Roc Solid Foundation, a local non-profit that builds hope for families fighting pediatric cancer. John also served the City of Chesapeake as a Planning Commissioner for five years, including leadership roles as Secretary and Vice-Chairman. In his free time, he enjoys the outdoors and loves spending time with his wife, two daughters, and two yellow labs.

John graduated from Regent University School of Law in 2010, where he served as Chairman of the Moot Court Board and a member of the Student Leader Advisory Board. After law school, John found his niche practicing real estate and business law throughout Virginia and North Carolina.

In real estate, John has experience representing investors, developers, builders, banks, lenders, and individual home buyers in a variety of transactions. He has handled transactions involving shopping centers, apartment complexes, retails stores and hotels.

John's business practice ranges from advising entrepreneurs to assisting established business owners in mergers, acquisitions, contracts, litigation and dispute resolution. He has worked with a variety of businesses ranging from small startups to an international multi-billion dollar corporation.

John is licensed to practice law in both Virginia and North Carolina.

attorneys.name: Deborah L. McIntyre
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law, Divorce, Custody, Support Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Debbie Mclntyre-Yurkovich is a founding partner of Mclntyre DeFede Law PLLC. Ms. Mclntyre has represented individuals in a variety of legal matters throughout Northern Virginia. Her clients benefit from her many years of experience in the legal field and the knowledge garnered from hundreds of prior cases and clients. As a parent, two of whom who has special needs, Ms. McIntyre understands the unique circumstances that present legally, economically, and emotionally to parents and their child(ren).

Ms. McIntyre is proud that many of her client referrals come from her many satisfied current and past clients. She is equally proud that she receives many referrals from opposing counsel, professional experts in the community, and former opposing parties.

Ms. McIntyre practices in the areas of family law, education (school) law, and adult guardianship law. She regularly appears in circuit and juvenile courts throughout Northern Virginia. She has extensive trial experience litigating complex equitable distribution tracing cases, relocation and international custody cases, protective order cases, abuse and neglect cases, and school law related matters. She also routinely represents individuals in school meetings and administrative proceedings, which include but are not limited to special education, in state tuition appeals, student discipline, and honor code violations. Ms. McIntyre also serves as counsel for those seeking guardianship and/or conservatorship of an incapacitated adult. She has also previously successfully represented hundreds of individuals charged with crimes ranging from misdemeanors to serious felonies.

Outside the practice of law, Ms. McIntyre has applied her skill set and background to previously serving as a School Board Member and Chair for Manassas Park City Schools.

attorneys.name: Claudia Melara Chase
attorneys.practice_type: Transactions Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
I offer a legal representation to businesses and individuals in a wide range of areas of law – transactions, litigation and immigration. I have experience representing clients in real estate, asset sales, and loan transactions. I have litigated matters in state courts, including breach of contract and tort liability claims. I have represented individuals affirmatively before the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and defensively before the Arlington Immigration Court. I have assisted my immigration clients with obtaining special immigrant juvenile status, residency and asylum.

I graduated with honors, magna cum laude, from Marymount University and then obtained my Juris Doctor from the University of Maryland School of Law. During law school, I completed a legal externship at the U.S. House of Representatives where I was awarded a Certificate of Congressional Recognition for developing guidelines in foreclosure prevention.

Prior to joining the firm, I worked as a litigator in private law firms and, before that, as a legal analyst at Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac). More recently, I practiced immigration law at Kids in Need of Defense (KIND).

I am licensed to practice law in federal and state courts in Virginia and the District of Columbia. I am a member of the Fairfax Bar Association and the American Immigration Lawyers Association. I am also a fluent Spanish speaker.

During my free time, I enjoy playing coed soccer. Throughout the years I have organized teams that have won indoor, outdoor and sand soccer championships. I also enjoy cooking. I am currently experimenting with outdoor, wood-fire cooking. Most of all, I enjoy family activities with my three wonderful children and husband.

attorneys.name: Dennis M. Mersberger
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Arlington, VA
attorneys.bio:
Dennis M. Mersberger founded Mersberger Criminal Defense, PLLC with a special interest in providing top notch criminal defense representation. He hails from the Philadelphia, Pennsylvania area, but has made Alexandria, Virginia his home and his office is located in Arlington, Virginia. Mr. Mersberger focuses his work almost exclusively on criminal trials in the state and federal courts. Mr. Mersberger has developed a reputation as a zealous criminal defense attorney, defending both adult and juvenile criminal and traffic matters.

For more than 20 years, Mr. Mersberger has handled cases throughout the Northern Virginia jurisdictions that include the City of Alexandria, Arlington County, Fairfax County, Falls Church, Fauquier, Loudoun County, the City of Manassas, Prince William County and Stafford as well as the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia in the Alexandria and Richmond Divisions of Virginia.

With a vision towards building a complete criminal and traffic defense practice, Mr. Mersberger has also appeared as appellate counsel in the Virginia Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Virginia. Mr. Mersberger is a member of the Criminal Law section of the Virginia State Bar, Virginia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (VACDL), and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL).

Active in his legal community, Mr. Mersberger served for many years as Committee Chair to the Alexandria Bar Association's Lawyer Referral Service and he currently serves as the Policy Board Chair for the Alexandria Alcohol Safety Action Program (ASAP).

Mr. Mersberger earned a Bachelor of Arts in English Literature from Lock Haven University of Pennsylvania and earned his J.D. from George Mason University School of Law. Mr. Mersberger is admitted to the Virginia State Bar, as well as to the bars of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia and the United States Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Tracy A. Meyer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fredericksburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Tracy A. Meyer is a Virginia family law attorney, having more than 23 years of experience in domestic relations matters representing her clients throughout Northern Virginia and surrounding areas including Prince William County, Stafford County, Spotsylvania County and the City of Fredericksburg.

Ms. Meyer aggressively represents her clients in all aspects of family law, including counseling and representing clients in the negotiation and drafting of prenuptial agreements, divorce, custody and visitation, support, division of marital assets, post-divorce modification and enforcement issues and protective orders. Ms. Meyer has also developed a special interest in mental health issues and divorce such as confidentiality and record-keeping.

Ms. Meyer is consistently recognized in Best Lawyers in America for Family Law and she has been selected for inclusion in Virginia Super Lawyers since 2012. She was also recognized as one of the "Top Divorce Lawyers" in Metropolitan Washington, D.C. in February 2009 by Washingtonian magazine. Ms. Meyer is rated "AV Preeminent" by Martindale-Hubbell, which is the highest peer rating that is given. She has been named as a Top Lawyer in 2017 by Northern Virginia Magazine and was selected as one of Virginia's Best Women Lawyers as published in Virginia Living in 2017. She has received the top rating possible, "Superb, 10 out of 10" from the Avvo ratings website.

Ms. Meyer is admitted to practice law in Virginia and the District of Columbia. She is the former co-chair of the Family Law Section of the Arlington County Bar Association and former chair of the Young Lawyers Section of the Arlington County Bar Association. She is a member of the Virginia State Bar Family Law Section, the Fairfax County Bar Association Family Law Section and the District of Columbia Bar.

Ms. Meyer graduated from the University of Northern Colorado, Honors Program, in 1992 (B.A., with departmental honors in Political Science, magna cum laude). In 1995, she received her law degree from the Washington College of Law, American University.

Ms. Meyer lives in Fredericksburg, Virginia with her husband and their three children. In her free time, she enjoys spending time with family and friends, working out, boating and movies.

Dan Miller grew up in the Chesapeake area of Virginia. He attended Norfolk Collegiate School, graduating in 1985. In 1987, he earned his Associates degree from Oxford College, where he majored in sociology and philosophy. Not too long after, Miller earned his Bachelor's degree in sociology and philosophy from Emory University.

From 1989 through 1995, Miller was the drummer in an Atlanta-based band, which went on tour throughout the southeast. Shortly after, Miller began his career at Michael I. Ashe, P.C., where he focused on criminal law and traffic violations.

In 2001, Miller began his own firm and now practice law in all Virginia courts, both federal and state. Due to his ceaseless efforts and passion to represent clients, he has been selected for inclusion into several professional legal organizations, including the Top 100 Trial Lawyers for Criminal Defense Lawyers in 2015. Miller also expanded his repertoire of practice to include family law cases stemming from Virginia domestic relations laws, such as divorce, child custody and support, domestic violence, and paternity cases.

attorneys.name: Eugene C. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Eugene "Gene" C. Miller has 35 years' experience combined in both personal injury defense and as a Plaintiff's attorney. Prior to joining the firm in 2010, he spent 25 years defending cases as the Managing Attorney for the office of GEICO Staff Counsel before choosing to represent victims of catastrophic injury and medical malpractice. Gene has extensive inside knowledge of insurance coverage issues and claim evaluation and handling processes and procedures. Since joining the firm and becoming a Partner in 2012, he has employed his unique perspective to offer valuable insight and experience critical in determining the best strategy for case negotiations, mediations, arbitrations, and trials, earning success for our clients and their families. Gene has extensive experience in personal injury litigation, having tried more than 180 jury trials in the various courts of Northern Virginia, including Federal Court, and in the Washington D.C. Superior Court.

Gene obtained a B.S. degree in Business from Virginia Tech, graduating with honors. He obtained his J.D. from George Mason University School of Law (now the Antonin Scalia Law School). During Law school, he was on the Jessup Moot Court team and interned with the Fairfax County Office of the Commonwealth’s Attorney. He also attended a Summer School of Law Program at the University of Exeter, England, sponsored by the Marshall Wythe School of Law of the College of William and Mary. He has been rated AV Preeminent® by Martindale-Hubble for over ten years due to his high ethical standards and professional ability.

Gene is active in the Fairfax Bar Association and is on the Circuit Court Committee and the Law Related Education Committee. He also participates as a Master of the Bench with the George Mason American Inn of Court. Additionally, he volunteers his time to speak to at-risk youth from local high schools and conduct court tours for middle school students.

Gene grew up in Fairfax County. He was a summer league and year-round AAU swimmer, summer lifeguard, pool manager, Red Cross swimming instructor and water safety instructor, and a swim coach. While raising his children, he coached house league softball teams. He currently resides in Leesburg with his wife, Glenda. He has six children, Darlene, James, Kaitlin, Brittany, Steven and Audrey, and four grandchildren, Briar, Skyler, Kieran, and Tim. He is an avid bicyclist, snow skier, and kayaker, and loves to fish.

attorneys.name: Heather Scott Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Mrs. Miller joined SSHW in 2015 and became a partner in the firm in 2022. She focuses solely on family law, and has done so her entire career. Mrs. Miller has successfully litigated cases in the areas of adultery, cruelty, abandonment, child support, spousal support, high asset division, business evaluation and division, high conflict custody and visitation, paternity, adoption, guardianship of incapacitated adults, CPS/DFS matters, and protective orders in cases of family abuse. She also takes cases representing children and incapacitated adults as a Guardian ad Litem.

Ms. Miller believes that it is important in family law cases to at least attempt to "calm the drama" and reduce the client's level of stress. She is a dedicated and persistent negotiator and has had tremendous success in settling cases outside of court. When that avenue is not a possibility Ms. Miller is a skilled litigator and oral advocate for her clients. She believes that preparation and attention to detail are the keys to presenting a persuasive case in court.

Ms. Miller is licensed to practice in the Commonwealth of Virginia. She takes cases in Loudoun County, Frederick County, Winchester City, and Clarke County.

In her free time, Ms. Miller chases her small daughter and watches Mickey Mouse Club House. She also has a beautiful Welsh Terrier pup named Lady Mary.

attorneys.name: Helena S. Mock Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: The Peninsula Center for Estate and Lifelong Planning
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Williamsburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Helena began her career as a legal clerk with the United States Army. In 2000, she graduated from the College of William & Mary School of Law in Williamsburg, Virginia, and began her practice with the law firm of Jones, Blechman, Woltz & Kelly, P.C. in Newport News, Virginia. In 2004, Helena became a full partner and later served as Chairman of the Estate Planning and Taxation Practice Group of the firm, supervising a team of attorneys, paralegals and other staff while attending to the needs of her many and varied estate planning and administration clients.

In May of 2010, Helena formed a law practice devoted to providing Virginia Peninsula clients with the best in estate, trust, and business planning: The Peninsula Center for Estate and Lifelong Planning, located in Williamsburg. She continues to provide the same breadth and quality of services to clients throughout Hampton Roads, including the Middle Peninsula and the Northern Neck.

Experience

Helena has extensive experience in advising clients on all facets of estate, tax, business, and long-term care planning to include establishing revocable and irrevocable trusts, charitable trusts, limited liability companies and family business limited partnerships, as well as drafting buy-sell agreements, shareholder agreements, marital agreements, wills, powers of attorney, medical directives, living wills and other estate planning documents necessary to protect clients both during lifetime and at death. She assists clients and their families with planning for future long-term care needs and in evaluating ways to protect and preserve assets. She advises clients on methods available for protecting assets from income, gift, estate, and generation-skipping transfer taxes and helps clients in preserving wealth for future generations. In addition, Helena helps clients deal with issues such as incapacity and death of a loved one and guides clients through the process of administering trusts and estates. She regularly practices before the local courts in instituting guardianships and conservatorships, reforming trusts and wills, and handling a variety of other matters involving wills, trusts, and estates. Helena also often serves in the capacity of executor or trustee and has frequently been appointed by local courts to serve as a fiduciary.

attorneys.name: Faisal Moghul Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Faisal Moghul stands out as one of Virginia’s top business lawyers, widely recognized for his extensive expertise in business formation and structuring, high-stakes business litigation involving both direct and derivative lawsuits, asset and stock sales, valuation and buyout disputes, and strategic asset protection. In 2023, he was named one of America’s Top 100 Civil Defense Litigators and was recognized as Virginia’s “Go-To” Business Lawyer. He has also made the prestigious Super Lawyers Rising Stars shortlist every year since 2016. In 2023, Moghul was recognized by Virginia Lawyer Magazine as one of the Commonwealth’s leading educators in business and real estate law, further solidifying his role as a thought leader in the legal community. Further, in 2024, Mr. Moghul spearheaded a litigation team that secured a landmark $565,000 judgment in a construction fraud case after a 4-day jury trial in Fairfax County Circuit Court.

Moghul’s client base, comprising of high-net-worth individuals, startups and emerging corporations, LLCs, and partnerships, consistently turns to him for his exceptional ability to handle complicated business and real estate matters with precision.

In 2023, Mr. Moghul was selected as the speaker and moderator at the Virginia CLE’s Annual Small Business Law Institute, where he presented on “Top 10 Clauses to Include in LLC Operating Agreements.” In 2024, Mr. Moghul was again selected to speak on “Protecting LLC Assets: Understanding Charging Orders and Asset Protection Strategies.” As a member of the American Bar Association’s (ABA) Committee on LLCs and Unincorporated Associations, Mr. Moghul’s comprehensive knowledge of various entity types – LLCs, S-Corps, C-Corps, and limited partnerships—coupled with his understanding of asset protection strategies, enables him to craft cutting-edge operating agreements, by laws, and partnership agreements that safeguard his clients’ interests.

As a veteran of more than 60 high-value transactions across the technology, real estate, government contracting and retail industries, he has overseen multimillion-dollar buyouts and redemptions for both majority and minority corporate shareholders, LLC members and LP partners. Moghul stands out not only for his business law expertise but also for his litigation successes. He is known for representing clients in high-stakes business litigation, including cases involving member/partner/shareholder derivative lawsuits, breach of fiduciary, fraud and defamation claims.

Similarly, Mr. Moghul is recognized as a top-tier real estate litigator with extensive experience in construction litigation, easement and boundary line disputes, real estate agent and broker representation, and purchase and sale contract disputes. He has successfully represented clients in high-stakes construction defect claims, often involving fraud and contractor negligence. His expertise in easement and boundary disputes has helped property owners resolve complex conflicts over land access and property rights.

In 2023, he also co-presented a CLE seminar on “Examining A Real Estate Broker’s Liability to the Purchaser In Residential Real Estate Transactions in Virginia,” a vital publication for understanding broker liability in Virginia, further establishing him as an authority on real estate agent and broker defense, including compliance with Virginia’s DPOR regulations.

Mr. Moghul has a deep knowledge of real estate purchase and sale contract disputes in Virginia, and has published several articles on this topic, including his 2021 critically acclaimed publication with the American Law Institute titled authored “Caveat Emptor vs. Seller Disclosure in Residential Real Property Conveyances,” which offers cutting-edge insights into the law surrounding purchase and sales of real property. Mr. Moghul’s deep understanding of the case law and regulations in this area of the law have enabled him to secure several million-dollar plus settlements and verdicts.

attorneys.name: Sheila Moheb
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Roanoke, VA
attorneys.bio:
Sheila Moheb is criminal and family law attorney serving the Commonwealth of Virginia She graduated with honors from the University of Richmond with a dual degree in English and Sociology. She then earned her Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Richmond School of Law, where she served as Editor-in-Chief of the Richmond Journal of Law and the Public interest.

As a criminal litigation attorney, Mrs. Moheb has served criminal defendants in over 25 jurisdictions across the Commonwealth, and she defends each client’s constitutional rights faithfully. As a second-generation Persian American, she prides herself in providing a voice for those who have been systematically muted or otherwise disregarded on the basis of their race, sex, gender or socioeconomic status. Mrs. Moheb has extensive jury trial experience, and she specializes in narcotics and weapons offenses, as well as violent sexual felonies.

While representing clients in domestic matters, Mrs. Moheb works effectively to mediate cases where litigation can and should be avoided. When litigation is inevitable, Mrs. Moheb is an aggressive yet efficient divorce attorney who seeks financial security and closure for her clients.

Prior to starting her firm, Sheila Moheb was a law clerk in the Virginia Court of Appeals for Justice Cleo E. Powell. Mrs. Moheb is a member of the Virginia Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the Virginia Women Attorneys Association, and she serves on the Board of Directors for Four Truths Recovery.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Mark Mokris, P.L.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in South Hill, VA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Mokris has been practicing law for over fifteen years. He graduated from Regent University School of Law in 1997 and in 1998 began his legal career as an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney for the County of Mecklenburg. During his time as a prosecutor he handled all types of prosecutions and for a short period of time was appointed to fill out the remainder of John White-Hurst's term as Commonwealth Attorney after Mr. White-Hurst's untimely death in office.

Mr. Mokris entered private practice in October of 2000 and has practiced with as many as three attorneys working as part of his law practice. Presently, he has downsized his practice to maximize his ability to focus on his clients rather than the additional duties of a larger law firm.

Since entering private practice, Mark Mokris, has defended many individuals in both judge and jury trials charged with murder, drug distribution crimes, sex offenses, and other serious types of cases. He has also co-taught, with Brendan Dunning, an online Virginia Continuing Legal Education Course on the Use of Experts in Criminal Cases and the implications of Melendez-Diaz.

Whether it is a simple traffic case or a complex murder case, custody and visitation, or some other legal problem Mr. Mokris utilizes his knowledge, expertise, and powerful online research engines to maximize the potential for a positive outcome.

attorneys.bio:
As an attorney, Zachary practices in all areas of family law, including property distribution, divorce, support, child custody disputes, protective orders, prenuptial agreements, and postnuptial agreements. Zachary was recognized as one of Virginia’s top practitioners under 40 by Thomson Reuter’s Super Lawyers in 2026.

As a resident of Arlington since 2020, Zachary is dedicated to serving families throughout the Northern Virginia community. Zachary regularly appears in Circuit and Juvenile Courts throughout Northern Virginia. Zachary has extensive experience appearing as an attorney for children in need of services (CHINS), and in child abuse & neglect cases appearing as both an attorney for parents and guardian ad litem for children.

Zachary earned his J.D. from George Mason University (Scalia) Law School in 2023. He received his Bachelors in History and Philosophy from Seton Hall University of New Jersey, in 2019, where he graduated magna cum laude. He is admitted to the Virginia State Bar, and is a member in good standing. Zachary has worked exclusively in the area of Family Law since 2021. Zachary worked for Schmergel & Mersberger, PLC throughout law school gaining experience on family law matters, while also serving as an editor on the George Mason International Law Journal, and as a member of the law school's alternative dispute resolution. Since being admitted to the bar Mr. Moore has continued to work alongside other members of the firm assisting clients in Arlington, Fairfax, Alexandria, and Prince William.

Outside the firm Zachary is active in the Northern Virginia legal community regularly attending events for the Arlington, Alexandria, & Fairfax bars along with his wife.

Prior to law school Mr. Moore worked as a research analyst at Financial Industry Technical Services, Inc.

attorneys.name: Christine Mougin
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations Litigation Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Christine Mougin-Boal has called western Loudoun County her home since 1988. Chris grew up in a multi-cultural home and lived in New York, Alaska and California. She is a fluent French speaker. Chris graduated from Colgate University in Hamilton, New York in 1982 and obtained her law degree from St. John’s University School of Law in New York in 1987. She has maintained licenses to practice law in Virginia, the District of Columbia and New York but currently practices solely in Virginia.

Chris began practicing law in 1988 in Fairfax, Virginia with a civil defense litigation firm focusing on personal injury and medical malpractice defense. In addition to litigating numerous cases, Chris prepared the majority of all appeals to the Virginia Supreme Court for the firm.

In 1994 she and her colleague Rhonda Paice established the firm of Paice & Mougin-Boal, P.C. in Leesburg, Virginia. In 2004 Paice and Mougin-Boal, P.C. merged with the Law Offices of Joe S. Ritenour, P.C. to form Ritenour, Paice & Mougin-Boal, a partnership of professional corporations. The firm then became Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton in 2010 with the addition of Jennifer Wexton as a partner. Sadly, in June of 2013, Joe S. Ritenour passed away unexpectedly. On January 1, 2015 Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton merged with Hendrix Demetriades P.C., the Law Offices of Daniel J. Travostino and the Law Offices of Thomas R. Rock to form The Laurel Brigade Law Group.

Since 1994, Chris’s practice includes all aspects of domestic relations litigation, including child custody and visitation, support issues, property division and divorce as well as appeals of domestic cases to the Court of Appeals. In addition, Chris does adoption work and adult guardianship and conservatorship cases. She has been qualified by the Virginia Supreme Court as a guardian ad litem for both children and incapacitated adults. Chris has also represented injured plaintiffs in personal injury and medical malpractice matters as well as individuals charged with traffic cases. She practices in all courts in Loudoun County and has been admitted in the past to practice in the Superior Court of the District of Columbia and the federal court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

In conjunction with practicing law, Chris has been actively involved in state and local bar associations. She is a Past President of the Virginia Women Attorneys Association (2010-2011) and Board Member of the state VWAA Board (2006-2014). Chris was one of the founding board members of the Loudoun Chapter of the VWAA, acting as Vice-President (2002-2003) and President (2004-2006) as well as Treasurer on two separate occasions. Through her association with the VWAA, Chris has spearheaded various pro bono and community based events including the local Adoption Day Program for Loudoun County and Empty Bowls Projects as well as a state-wide conference in 2010 entitled Diversity and the Practice of Law: New Clients, New Perspectives, New Challenges.

During her time practicing in Loudoun, Chris has consistently participated in local bar activities. She has been an active member of the Loudoun County Bar Association and chaired a program in the mid 1990’s where middle school and high school students presented mock trials before local judges. Chris has also been the Treasurer of the Loudon County Bar Association and has been a member of the Board of Directors for the terms 1995-1996 and 2005-2006.

Chris has also devoted her time to Virginia State Bar activities. From 2006-2012 she was a member of the Special Committee on Lawyer Referral, a service designed to assist the public in obtaining referrals for local attorneys. In 2013 Chris began a three year elected term as a member of the Virginia State Bar Council, the body generally charged with the administration of the affairs of the Virginia State Bar. In 2013 Chris was invited to begin a three year term as faculty member for Virginia State Bar’s Harry L. Carrico Professionalism Class, the Virginia Supreme Court’s mandatory course on Professionalism and the Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct.

Chris is a partner in Marquis Investment, LLC. The Laurel Brigade, a former inn, was carefully renovated and restored by Marquis Investments, LLC. The Law Offices of Ritenour Paice & Mougin-Boal opened their offices in this historic site in December of 2004 and as of January 1, 2015, the Laurel Brigade is now the proud home of Marquis Law Group.

attorneys.bio:
David began practicing law in 1973 and was admitted to the Bars of the District of Columbia and Virginia that same year. He has maintained an office in Fall Church and Leesburg for most of his career. During 1970’s and 1980’s David handled both criminal and civil litigation in both the State and Federal courts. During this time he also formed several law partnerships as members of the firms became prosecutors and judges.

In recent years, David has continued to handle complex civil litigation including breach of contract, real estate disputes, lender compliance and toxic mold.

Since the enactment of the Virginia Land Preservation Tax Credit legislation, Moyes Hanssen Overson, PLLC has concentrated on the drafting of conservation and open space easements and the filing for various tax forms related to the easements. During the period from 2007 through 2010 the firm has participated in the preparation and qualification of easements in excess of $200 million in Federal charitable gifts and $75 million in Virginia tax credits.

In addition to the conservation work, Moyes Hanssen Overson, PLLC represent lenders and borrowers in real estate and business sales and purchases.

attorneys.name: Alexandra "Sandy" D. Bowen
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Sandy Bowen, a founding partner at Bowen, Ten, Long, & Bal, PC, has concentrated her practice on family law and representing families in separation and divorce since 1988. She brings years of professional experience and her extensive network of resources to each client's case. Sandy assists her clients in achieving their goals while respecting their dignity and resources.

Sandy's personal experience with divorce when her daughter was 4 years old has provided her with an added level of sensitivity to her family law clients' needs. Sandy has a special appreciation for just how personal the divorce experience is for her clients and the long-term impact the divorce litigation process can have on family relationships. It is important to her that clients receive good value for the money they spend on legal representation. Sandy recognizes that family law litigation can be a frustrating and expensive experience. She helps prepare and guide her clients through this difficult time with care and discretion.

Sandy begins her work with each client by identifying their goals. She informs her clients about the court process, educates them about the law, and assists them in identifying the factual evidence that is necessary to put the best case before the court should a settlement not be reached.

Sandy knows it is important to educate clients about the legal process and help them understand what they can realistically expect when the court system is involved in deciding what is best for their children and finances. This education is crucial to ensuring that clients receive good value for the money they spend on legal representation.

Sandy was a founding partner at Bowen, Champlin, Foreman & Rockecharlie in Chesterfield County, Virginia, and managed that firm from 1997 to 2006. From 2006 until February 2014, she was with Coates & Davenport, P.C. in Richmond. This experience supports her practice of representing all parties in divorce litigation involving complex financial issues.

Sandy is from Arlington County. She graduated from the University of Virginia and later earned her law degree from the TC Williams School of Law at the University of Richmond. Sandy is a member of several professional organizations, including the Virginia State Bar, the Chesterfield County Bar Association, the Henrico County Bar Association, the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, the Metro Richmond Family Law Bar Association, and the Metropolitan Richmond Women's Bar Association, where she has previously held the positions of Secretary and Treasurer. She is admitted to practice in all courts in the Commonwealth of Virginia and federal courts, including the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Sandy takes great pride in her family, which includes two grown children. She has been actively involved in various school and community organizations, often serving on their Board of Directors. Additionally, Sandy has volunteered for many years with the Virginia Bar Association, helping staff Central Virginia Legal Aid's Hot Line with volunteer attorneys. She continues to support the pro bono initiatives of the Virginia Bar Association, ensuring that legal services are accessible, and advises clients referred by the Legal Information Network for Cancer (LINC).

attorneys.name: Christine Mougin
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations Litigation Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Christine Mougin-Boal has called western Loudoun County her home since 1988. Chris grew up in a multi-cultural home and lived in New York, Alaska and California. She is a fluent French speaker. Chris graduated from Colgate University in Hamilton, New York in 1982 and obtained her law degree from St. John’s University School of Law in New York in 1987. She has maintained licenses to practice law in Virginia, the District of Columbia and New York but currently practices solely in Virginia.

Chris began practicing law in 1988 in Fairfax, Virginia with a civil defense litigation firm focusing on personal injury and medical malpractice defense. In addition to litigating numerous cases, Chris prepared the majority of all appeals to the Virginia Supreme Court for the firm.

In 1994 she and her colleague Rhonda Paice established the firm of Paice & Mougin-Boal, P.C. in Leesburg, Virginia. In 2004 Paice and Mougin-Boal, P.C. merged with the Law Offices of Joe S. Ritenour, P.C. to form Ritenour, Paice & Mougin-Boal, a partnership of professional corporations. The firm then became Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton in 2010 with the addition of Jennifer Wexton as a partner. Sadly, in June of 2013, Joe S. Ritenour passed away unexpectedly. On January 1, 2015 Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton merged with Hendrix Demetriades P.C., the Law Offices of Daniel J. Travostino and the Law Offices of Thomas R. Rock to form The Laurel Brigade Law Group.

Since 1994, Chris’s practice includes all aspects of domestic relations litigation, including child custody and visitation, support issues, property division and divorce as well as appeals of domestic cases to the Court of Appeals. In addition, Chris does adoption work and adult guardianship and conservatorship cases. She has been qualified by the Virginia Supreme Court as a guardian ad litem for both children and incapacitated adults. Chris has also represented injured plaintiffs in personal injury and medical malpractice matters as well as individuals charged with traffic cases. She practices in all courts in Loudoun County and has been admitted in the past to practice in the Superior Court of the District of Columbia and the federal court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

In conjunction with practicing law, Chris has been actively involved in state and local bar associations. She is a Past President of the Virginia Women Attorneys Association (2010-2011) and Board Member of the state VWAA Board (2006-2014). Chris was one of the founding board members of the Loudoun Chapter of the VWAA, acting as Vice-President (2002-2003) and President (2004-2006) as well as Treasurer on two separate occasions. Through her association with the VWAA, Chris has spearheaded various pro bono and community based events including the local Adoption Day Program for Loudoun County and Empty Bowls Projects as well as a state-wide conference in 2010 entitled Diversity and the Practice of Law: New Clients, New Perspectives, New Challenges.

During her time practicing in Loudoun, Chris has consistently participated in local bar activities. She has been an active member of the Loudoun County Bar Association and chaired a program in the mid 1990’s where middle school and high school students presented mock trials before local judges. Chris has also been the Treasurer of the Loudon County Bar Association and has been a member of the Board of Directors for the terms 1995-1996 and 2005-2006.

Chris has also devoted her time to Virginia State Bar activities. From 2006-2012 she was a member of the Special Committee on Lawyer Referral, a service designed to assist the public in obtaining referrals for local attorneys. In 2013 Chris began a three year elected term as a member of the Virginia State Bar Council, the body generally charged with the administration of the affairs of the Virginia State Bar. In 2013 Chris was invited to begin a three year term as faculty member for Virginia State Bar’s Harry L. Carrico Professionalism Class, the Virginia Supreme Court’s mandatory course on Professionalism and the Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct.

Chris is a partner in Marquis Investment, LLC. The Laurel Brigade, a former inn, was carefully renovated and restored by Marquis Investments, LLC. The Law Offices of Ritenour Paice & Mougin-Boal opened their offices in this historic site in December of 2004 and as of January 1, 2015, the Laurel Brigade is now the proud home of Marquis Law Group.

attorneys.bio:
Griffin O'Hanlon joined Cooper Hurley Injury Lawyers as an attorney in the fall of 2015. He attended Great Bridge High School in Chesapeake for his freshman and sophomore years, before his parents relocated to Illinois. He returned to Virginia to attend Virginia Tech, where he majored in history. Griff obtained his J.D. from the Saint Louis University School of Law with a concentration in civil litigation.

After law school, Griff returned to Hampton Roads and now lives in Virginia Beach. He practiced criminal law at the Norfolk Public Defender's Office and a local private firm before joining Cooper Hurley and has extensive in-court litigation experience. Griff recently married Kelsey O'Hanlon (formerly Turner), a graduate of Tallwood High School in Virginia Beach who works as a speech therapist for the Virginia Beach Public Schools. When he's not working on his files, Griff can be found on the beach, golf course or cheering on Virginia Tech's football team.

Lawrence M. Schonberger is a principal of Sevila, Saunders, Huddleston & White, P.C. Mr. Schonberger's practice emphasizes real estate, commercial transactions, small business corporations, foreclosures, and community association law He served two terms (1997-2000; 2000-2003) on the Board of Governors for the Real Property Section of the Virginia State Bar, during which he served as Secretary (1999-2000), Vice-Chair (2000-2001) and Chair (2001-2002) of the board. He has been designated one of Virginia's "Legal Elite" on numerous occasions by Virginia Business Magazine. Mr. Schonberger has also received a peer review rating of AV from Martindale-Hubbell.

attorneys.name: Kimberly Waletich
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Falls Church, VA
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly Waletich is a contract attorney with Maddox & Gerock in Falls Church, Virginia, and has been working with the firm since October 2016. Kim was licensed in 2006 and has represented clients in equitable distribution, spousal support, child support, custody, visitation and relocation matters.

Kim understands that the divorce of a family is often one of the most traumatic events someone will have to endure. She sees her role as not just an attorney, but also as a counselor at law. She strives to help her clients through the divorce process quickly and respectfully while preserving what is good in their family relationship. Kim also draws on her business experience to help clients assess costs and benefits with various strategies through the process.

Kim began her legal career as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable William T. Newman, Jr., the Honorable Benjamin N.A. Kendrick, the Honorable Joanne F. Alper, and the Honorable James F. Almand of the Arlington County Circuit Court, 17th Judicial Circuit of Virginia. Kim then joined the family law firm of Condo, Roop, Kelly & Byrnes, P.C., where she was an associate attorney. When David Roop decided to form The Roop Law Firm, PLLC, Kim joined him as the firm’s founding associate attorney. Kim left that firm in 2012 and spent four years raising her son.

Kim earned her law degree, cum laude, in 2006 from American University’s Washington College of Law where she was editor-in-chief of the Business Law Brief and a member of the Administrative Law Review, the American Bar Association’s publication on administrative law. Kim served as a student attorney in the Civil Practice Clinical Program, where she received the highest-grade award for her fieldwork. In 2005, Kim served as a legal intern with the Virginia Supreme Court’s Office of the Chief Staff Attorney. Kim also studied Comparative International Law with the law school’s London-Paris-Geneva program.

Prior to law school, Kim worked for The Washington Post and Washingtonpost.Newsweek Interactive as an advertising account executive from 1999 until 2003, where she earned the President’s Club Award in 2001 and 2002 as one of the top 15 account executives in the company.

Kim graduated from James Madison University in 1999, where she earned a B.A., cum laude, in international affairs with a minor in political science.

Kim was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and grew up in Lincoln, Nebraska. Although she grew up a Cornhusker, she’s replaced college football with Washington Nationals baseball. She lives in Arlington with her husband (Alex), son (Wylie) and their 18-year-old cat (Gordon, a.k.a. G. Gordon Kitty).

attorneys.name: Alexandra "Sandy" D. Bowen
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Sandy Bowen, a founding partner at Bowen, Ten, Long, & Bal, PC, has concentrated her practice on family law and representing families in separation and divorce since 1988. She brings years of professional experience and her extensive network of resources to each client's case. Sandy assists her clients in achieving their goals while respecting their dignity and resources.

Sandy's personal experience with divorce when her daughter was 4 years old has provided her with an added level of sensitivity to her family law clients' needs. Sandy has a special appreciation for just how personal the divorce experience is for her clients and the long-term impact the divorce litigation process can have on family relationships. It is important to her that clients receive good value for the money they spend on legal representation. Sandy recognizes that family law litigation can be a frustrating and expensive experience. She helps prepare and guide her clients through this difficult time with care and discretion.

Sandy begins her work with each client by identifying their goals. She informs her clients about the court process, educates them about the law, and assists them in identifying the factual evidence that is necessary to put the best case before the court should a settlement not be reached.

Sandy knows it is important to educate clients about the legal process and help them understand what they can realistically expect when the court system is involved in deciding what is best for their children and finances. This education is crucial to ensuring that clients receive good value for the money they spend on legal representation.

Sandy was a founding partner at Bowen, Champlin, Foreman & Rockecharlie in Chesterfield County, Virginia, and managed that firm from 1997 to 2006. From 2006 until February 2014, she was with Coates & Davenport, P.C. in Richmond. This experience supports her practice of representing all parties in divorce litigation involving complex financial issues.

Sandy is from Arlington County. She graduated from the University of Virginia and later earned her law degree from the TC Williams School of Law at the University of Richmond. Sandy is a member of several professional organizations, including the Virginia State Bar, the Chesterfield County Bar Association, the Henrico County Bar Association, the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, the Metro Richmond Family Law Bar Association, and the Metropolitan Richmond Women's Bar Association, where she has previously held the positions of Secretary and Treasurer. She is admitted to practice in all courts in the Commonwealth of Virginia and federal courts, including the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Sandy takes great pride in her family, which includes two grown children. She has been actively involved in various school and community organizations, often serving on their Board of Directors. Additionally, Sandy has volunteered for many years with the Virginia Bar Association, helping staff Central Virginia Legal Aid's Hot Line with volunteer attorneys. She continues to support the pro bono initiatives of the Virginia Bar Association, ensuring that legal services are accessible, and advises clients referred by the Legal Information Network for Cancer (LINC).

attorneys.name: Christine Mougin
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations Litigation Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Christine Mougin-Boal has called western Loudoun County her home since 1988. Chris grew up in a multi-cultural home and lived in New York, Alaska and California. She is a fluent French speaker. Chris graduated from Colgate University in Hamilton, New York in 1982 and obtained her law degree from St. John’s University School of Law in New York in 1987. She has maintained licenses to practice law in Virginia, the District of Columbia and New York but currently practices solely in Virginia.

Chris began practicing law in 1988 in Fairfax, Virginia with a civil defense litigation firm focusing on personal injury and medical malpractice defense. In addition to litigating numerous cases, Chris prepared the majority of all appeals to the Virginia Supreme Court for the firm.

In 1994 she and her colleague Rhonda Paice established the firm of Paice & Mougin-Boal, P.C. in Leesburg, Virginia. In 2004 Paice and Mougin-Boal, P.C. merged with the Law Offices of Joe S. Ritenour, P.C. to form Ritenour, Paice & Mougin-Boal, a partnership of professional corporations. The firm then became Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton in 2010 with the addition of Jennifer Wexton as a partner. Sadly, in June of 2013, Joe S. Ritenour passed away unexpectedly. On January 1, 2015 Ritenour Paice Mougin-Boal & Wexton merged with Hendrix Demetriades P.C., the Law Offices of Daniel J. Travostino and the Law Offices of Thomas R. Rock to form The Laurel Brigade Law Group.

Since 1994, Chris’s practice includes all aspects of domestic relations litigation, including child custody and visitation, support issues, property division and divorce as well as appeals of domestic cases to the Court of Appeals. In addition, Chris does adoption work and adult guardianship and conservatorship cases. She has been qualified by the Virginia Supreme Court as a guardian ad litem for both children and incapacitated adults. Chris has also represented injured plaintiffs in personal injury and medical malpractice matters as well as individuals charged with traffic cases. She practices in all courts in Loudoun County and has been admitted in the past to practice in the Superior Court of the District of Columbia and the federal court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

In conjunction with practicing law, Chris has been actively involved in state and local bar associations. She is a Past President of the Virginia Women Attorneys Association (2010-2011) and Board Member of the state VWAA Board (2006-2014). Chris was one of the founding board members of the Loudoun Chapter of the VWAA, acting as Vice-President (2002-2003) and President (2004-2006) as well as Treasurer on two separate occasions. Through her association with the VWAA, Chris has spearheaded various pro bono and community based events including the local Adoption Day Program for Loudoun County and Empty Bowls Projects as well as a state-wide conference in 2010 entitled Diversity and the Practice of Law: New Clients, New Perspectives, New Challenges.

During her time practicing in Loudoun, Chris has consistently participated in local bar activities. She has been an active member of the Loudoun County Bar Association and chaired a program in the mid 1990’s where middle school and high school students presented mock trials before local judges. Chris has also been the Treasurer of the Loudon County Bar Association and has been a member of the Board of Directors for the terms 1995-1996 and 2005-2006.

Chris has also devoted her time to Virginia State Bar activities. From 2006-2012 she was a member of the Special Committee on Lawyer Referral, a service designed to assist the public in obtaining referrals for local attorneys. In 2013 Chris began a three year elected term as a member of the Virginia State Bar Council, the body generally charged with the administration of the affairs of the Virginia State Bar. In 2013 Chris was invited to begin a three year term as faculty member for Virginia State Bar’s Harry L. Carrico Professionalism Class, the Virginia Supreme Court’s mandatory course on Professionalism and the Virginia Rules of Professional Conduct.

Chris is a partner in Marquis Investment, LLC. The Laurel Brigade, a former inn, was carefully renovated and restored by Marquis Investments, LLC. The Law Offices of Ritenour Paice & Mougin-Boal opened their offices in this historic site in December of 2004 and as of January 1, 2015, the Laurel Brigade is now the proud home of Marquis Law Group.

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Falls Church, VA
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly Waletich is a contract attorney with Maddox & Gerock in Falls Church, Virginia, and has been working with the firm since October 2016. Kim was licensed in 2006 and has represented clients in equitable distribution, spousal support, child support, custody, visitation and relocation matters.

Kim understands that the divorce of a family is often one of the most traumatic events someone will have to endure. She sees her role as not just an attorney, but also as a counselor at law. She strives to help her clients through the divorce process quickly and respectfully while preserving what is good in their family relationship. Kim also draws on her business experience to help clients assess costs and benefits with various strategies through the process.

Kim began her legal career as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable William T. Newman, Jr., the Honorable Benjamin N.A. Kendrick, the Honorable Joanne F. Alper, and the Honorable James F. Almand of the Arlington County Circuit Court, 17th Judicial Circuit of Virginia. Kim then joined the family law firm of Condo, Roop, Kelly & Byrnes, P.C., where she was an associate attorney. When David Roop decided to form The Roop Law Firm, PLLC, Kim joined him as the firm’s founding associate attorney. Kim left that firm in 2012 and spent four years raising her son.

Kim earned her law degree, cum laude, in 2006 from American University’s Washington College of Law where she was editor-in-chief of the Business Law Brief and a member of the Administrative Law Review, the American Bar Association’s publication on administrative law. Kim served as a student attorney in the Civil Practice Clinical Program, where she received the highest-grade award for her fieldwork. In 2005, Kim served as a legal intern with the Virginia Supreme Court’s Office of the Chief Staff Attorney. Kim also studied Comparative International Law with the law school’s London-Paris-Geneva program.

Prior to law school, Kim worked for The Washington Post and Washingtonpost.Newsweek Interactive as an advertising account executive from 1999 until 2003, where she earned the President’s Club Award in 2001 and 2002 as one of the top 15 account executives in the company.

Kim graduated from James Madison University in 1999, where she earned a B.A., cum laude, in international affairs with a minor in political science.

Kim was born in St. Louis, Missouri, and grew up in Lincoln, Nebraska. Although she grew up a Cornhusker, she’s replaced college football with Washington Nationals baseball. She lives in Arlington with her husband (Alex), son (Wylie) and their 18-year-old cat (Gordon, a.k.a. G. Gordon Kitty).

Casey Nash is a consumer law attorney who has practiced exclusively in the field of consumer protection for her entire legal career. She represents clients in Virginia and Washington, D.C. on a variety of matters, including credit reporting, inaccurate or misleading employment background reports, abusive debt collection practices, mortgage servicing, predatory lending, and TCPA issues.

Casey has significant litigation experience, including over 250 federal cases and dozens of complex, class-action cases. She has consistently been recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers magazine. She has also taught and trained lawyers and legal aid organizations on consumer protection laws.

During her law school career, she worked for several civil litigation firms and served as a law clerk for a judge at the Office of Administrative Hearings in Washington, D.C.

Casey lives in Northern Virginia with her husband and Great Dane, Reagan.

attorneys.name: Nicole H. Naum Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Naum is a highly respected criminal defense attorney based in Manassas, Virginia, with over 15 years of experience representing clients throughout Northern Virginia. As the founder of Battlefield Law Group, PLLC, Nicole is known for her unwavering commitment to defending individuals facing both misdemeanor and felony charges, with a strong focus on DUI defense.

Nicole has earned a powerful reputation in DUI law, driven by her passion for protecting clients from the serious consequences of impaired driving charges. She regularly attends national DUI defense seminars and advanced training to stay on the cutting edge of changes in DUI laws, enforcement tactics, and scientific developments in breath and blood testing. Whether defending a first-time DUI or a complex felony-level case, Nicole combines deep legal knowledge with relentless advocacy.

She is well known and respected by the prosecutors and judges, across Prince William, Fairfax, Loudoun, Arlington, Culpeper, Stafford, and Fauquier Counties. This regional insight allows her to tailor strategies that are not just legally sound, but courtroom-specific and effective.

Nicole earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law in 2008 and has dedicated her entire legal career to criminal defense. Her academic background in Mathematical Sciences from the University of Michigan gives her a unique edge in analyzing technical evidence, such as toxicology reports, breathalyzer data, and body cam footage, especially critical in DUI and other scientifically based cases.

Her approach is strategic, detail-oriented, and client-focused. She understands how overwhelming criminal charges can be and works closely with each client to guide them through the process with clarity, respect, and tireless advocacy. Whether in negotiations or at trial, Nicole brings depth, focus, and tenacity to every case.

Nicole’s excellence has earned her numerous accolades, including multiple selections to Super Lawyers Rising Stars (2014, 2015, 2018–2022), Prince William County General District Court Attorney of the Year (2013), and most recently, The National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Criminal Defense Attorneys (2024). Her firm, Battlefield Law Group, PLLC, was also named Best Law Firm in Manassas by Business Rate.

A professional woman in a business suit stands confidently against a blue background on the right side. On the left side, there is a testimonial praising "Ms. Naum" for going above and beyond, along with a five-star rating, attributed to "Angela L." from Google 2025.

sections.content:
Nicole Naum is a highly respected criminal defense attorney based in Manassas, Virginia, with over 15 years of experience representing clients throughout Northern Virginia. As the founder of Battlefield Law Group, PLLC, Nicole is known for her unwavering commitment to defending individuals facing both misdemeanor and felony charges, with a strong focus on DUI defense.

Nicole has earned a powerful reputation in DUI law, driven by her passion for protecting clients from the serious consequences of impaired driving charges. She regularly attends national DUI defense seminars and advanced training to stay on the cutting edge of changes in DUI laws, enforcement tactics, and scientific developments in breath and blood testing. Whether defending a first-time DUI or a complex felony-level case, Nicole combines deep legal knowledge with relentless advocacy.

She is well known and respected by the prosecutors and judges, across Prince William, Fairfax, Loudoun, Arlington, Culpeper, Stafford, and Fauquier Counties. This regional insight allows her to tailor strategies that are not just legally sound, but courtroom-specific and effective.

Nicole earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law in 2008 and has dedicated her entire legal career to criminal defense. Her academic background in Mathematical Sciences from the University of Michigan gives her a unique edge in analyzing technical evidence, such as toxicology reports, breathalyzer data, and body cam footage, especially critical in DUI and other scientifically based cases.

Her approach is strategic, detail-oriented, and client-focused. She understands how overwhelming criminal charges can be and works closely with each client to guide them through the process with clarity, respect, and tireless advocacy. Whether in negotiations or at trial, Nicole brings depth, focus, and tenacity to every case.

Nicole’s excellence has earned her numerous accolades, including multiple selections to Super Lawyers Rising Stars (2014, 2015, 2018–2022), Prince William County General District Court Attorney of the Year (2013), and most recently, The National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Criminal Defense Attorneys (2024). Her firm, Battlefield Law Group, PLLC, was also named Best Law Firm in Manassas by Business Rate.

A professional woman in a business suit stands confidently against a blue background on the right side. On the left side, there is a testimonial praising "Ms. Naum" for going above and beyond, along with a five-star rating, attributed to "Angela L." from Google 2025.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fredericksburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Junior Ndlovu has a passion for helping clients when they are most in need. After taking on a pro bono case to help a disadvantaged family, he decided to become a plaintiff's trial attorney in personal injury. He establishes trust with his clients, building stronger relationships.

Advocacy competitions have given Junior an edge when it comes to the courtroom. He brings to the table a strong confidence that comes from debating law and winning oral advocacy competitions. He primarily works out of the Fredericksburg office.

In his free time, Junior loves to play chess, take long walks, and listen to audiobooks. He grew up in Zimbabwe and came to the U.S. to attend college and law school. In law school, Junior met his wife, Natey. Her experience coming to the U.S. as a refugee from the Congo has inspired Junior to help build stronger support systems within immigrant communities. Junior and Natey enjoy traveling and entertaining friends.

attorneys.name: Nolan R. Nicely Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Covington, VA
attorneys.bio:
Nolan is a native of Alleghany County, born and raised east of Clifton Forge. He graduated from Hampden-Sydney College, summa cum laude, in 1991, and received his juris doctorate from the University of Virginia School of Law in 1994. After law school, Nolan returned to his hometown and has practiced law with Russ Updike since 1994. Nolan's legal practice has primarily focused on complex civil litigation, with particular focus on information discovery, legal research/writing, liens, insurance coverage and other issues related to navigating the information intensive environment of modern complex personal injury and medical malpractice cases.

Nolan has been active in his Church and multiple community organizations over the years. He has a special interest in land and wildlife management and he and his wife, Hope, own the Grizzled Skipper Conservation Ranch in western Alleghany County. They live in the Sharon area, east of Clifton Forge, with their two sons, Nolan III and Asher.

attorneys.name: Kaveh Noorishad
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Litigation Lawyers in McLean, VA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Kaveh Noorishad concentrates his practice in criminal and civil litigation and practices throughout all Virginia state courts as well as the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia. He has defended a wide variety of criminal matters ranging from minor traffic offenses to serious felony charges. In addition to his criminal practice, Mr. Noorishad has also litigated several multi-million dollar civil actions involving personal injury, professional liability, construction litigation, and toxic torts.

Mr. Noorishad understands that the litigation process can be an unsettling and stressful process so he strives to keep his clients informed at every step of the litigation process to reduce the anxiety that often accompanies litigation. Mr. Noorishad prides himself on thoroughly preparing his cases, providing regular status updates to his clients and returning telephone calls promptly.

Mr. Noorishad earned his Bachelor of Arts, with honors, in International Business from the American University in Washington, D.C. in 2001, his Masters in Business Administration, summa cum laude, from the American University in Washington, D.C. in 2003, and his Juris Doctor from the Georgetown University Law Center in 2006. While attending law school, Mr. Noorishad was a member of the Georgetown Journal of Legal Ethics and published "The Sarbanes-Oxley Act and Its Effect on In-House Legal Counsel", 18 Geo. J. Ethics 1041(2005).

Mr. Noorishad is admitted to practice in Virginia and California. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Virginia Bar Association, the Fairfax Bar Association, the Virginia Young Lawyers Conference, and the California Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Charles J. (C.J.) Nucciarone Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Charles J. Nucciarone, or C.J., as he is known around the office, has represented individuals all over the Commonwealth of Virginia in both state and federal courts in a variety of DWI/DUI, criminal, traffic, and injury cases. C.J.’s criminal, DWI/DUI, and traffic defense experience includes low-level traffic citations (like speeding), more serious traffic matters like reckless driving and DWI/DUI, misdemeanor criminal offenses like assault and battery, shoplifting, and domestic violence, to the most serious felony crimes including violent crime, drug possession and distribution, homicide, and sexually-based offenses.

C.J. has also represented numerous clients in injury claims arising from car collisions. Having spent years working for some of the largest insurance companies in the country, C.J. puts that knowledge to use for his clients in obtaining fair and full compensation for the injuries, pain, and suffering that they experience due to someone else’s negligence.

It is C.J.’s mission to provide quality, effective legal representation to those facing criminal accusations or dealing with the consequences of someone else’s negligence in his native home of Northern Virginia, the Virginia Piedmont Region, and the Shenandoah Valley. he has obtained “not guilty” verdicts in a variety of criminal and traffic cases and has negotiated favorable resolutions in countless others.

attorneys.name: Lili R. O'Connell Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Protective Orders Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Lili O’Connell is a passionate and sharp criminal defense attorney with a strong track record of success in courts throughout Northern Virginia. Known for her agility in the courtroom and her unwavering commitment to her clients, Lili brings deep experience across criminal, domestic, and civil matters. She is especially skilled in navigating high-stakes cases involving Protective Orders, DUI/DWI, and misdemeanor and felony criminal charges, where her strategic thinking and strong courtroom presence consistently deliver results.

Lili’s legal practice spans across all jurisdictions in Northern Virginia, including Fairfax, Culpeper, Fauquier, Alexandria, Prince William, Stafford, and Loudoun. She has represented clients in General District, Circuit, and Juvenile & Domestic Relations Courts, earning a reputation among judges and opposing counsel as a prepared, persuasive, and principled advocate.

What truly sets Lili apart is her combination of legal precision and human empathy. She listens carefully to her clients’ concerns and provides straightforward, honest guidance every step of the way. Whether defending someone charged with a serious criminal offense or advocating for a protective order to keep them safe, she approaches each case with diligence, compassion, and fierce advocacy.

In addition to her extensive experience in criminal defense, Lili is a certified Guardian ad Litem for the Commonwealth of Virginia, where she advocates for the best interests of children in custody disputes, abuse and neglect cases, and juvenile delinquency matters. Her work in this role reflects her deep commitment to protecting vulnerable individuals within the legal system.

A native of New England, Lili earned both her Juris Doctor and her Bachelor of Arts from the University of Connecticut, where she developed a strong foundation in legal advocacy and public service. She is an active member of the Virginia State Bar and maintains strong professional ties through her involvement in the Fairfax Bar Association and the Prince William Bar Association.

When she’s not in the courtroom, Lili enjoys spending quality time with her husband, their children, and their two dogs. She is also an avid equestrian and finds balance and fulfillment in horseback riding and outdoor activities.

attorneys.name: Colin O'Dawe
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Norfolk, VA
attorneys.bio:
Colin grew up in a military family throughout the US and Europe before graduating from high school on the Peninsula.

Colin received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Virginia Tech in 2003, and his Juris Doctor from George Mason School of Law in 2006.

In Law School, Colin worked as a law clerk for a law firm in Northern Virginia specializing in personal injury litigation, and interned at the United States Department of Justice in our Nation's Capital. Additionally, Colin was a member of George Mason's Law Review.

After graduating from Law School, Colin returned to Hampton Roads and practiced as a trial lawyer for five years at the Office of the Public Defender for the City of Norfolk.

There, Colin zealously represented his clients charged with every class of criminal offenses ranging from misdemeanors to first degree murder in hundreds of bench trials and numerous jury trials.

Colin's area of Practice includes Personal Injury Litigation and Criminal Defense. He is an active member of the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association (VTLA) and the Virginia State Bar. When away from the office, Colin enjoys snow skiing, boating with family on the Chesapeake Bay, and traveling with his wife.

attorneys.name: Dexter S. Odin
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate & Land Use Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
A founding member of Odin, Feldman & Pittleman PC, Dexter Odin has been practicing law for over 50 years and has a keen understanding of his clients' situations. Leveraging his knowledge of the law and substantial experience, he provides practical solutions that are as innovative and unique as his diverse client base. His experience includes land use, municipal law, and commercial and criminal litigation.

Dexter has tried criminal and civil cases involving most every form of business organization and controversy ranging from trademarks, federal tax issues, and business fraud to contract, tort, and entity and officer controversies. His federal trial practice has included cases arising under treaty and international law as well as the representation of the Republic of Sudan.

From being the court-appointed counselor assigned to defend the leader of a storied motorcycle club against charges of torture and double murder to securing multi-million dollar verdicts in his clients' favor, Dexter has been a powerful advocate for justice throughout his career. But his specialty, as it were, has come to be the wisdom and experience his clients and the many boards and committees on which he has served on throughout the years have so generously provided to him.

attorneys.name: Kara G. Osborne
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Osborne’s federal practice focuses on cases before various administrative agencies — including the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB), Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), and Office of Personnel Management (OPM) – as well as security clearance cases before the Defense Office of Hearings and Appeals (DOHA), the Department of Defense Central Adjudication Facility (DoD CAF) and other federal agencies. Ms. Osborne also focuses on various administrative matters involving federal law enforcement officers.

Ms. Osborne works closely with and advises clients on various federal retirement matters, including OPM disability retirement applications; Federal Erroneous Retirement Coverage Act (FERCCA) corrections; law enforcement, firefighter, and air traffic controller special retirement coverage; court-ordered benefits; and general Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS), Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS), and CSRS Offset retirement issues.

In addition, Ms. Osborne advises private sector and municipal employees in the District of Columbia in various types of investigations, grievance procedures, disciplinary actions, whistleblower issues, and equal employment opportunity (EEO) matters.

Prior to joining the firm, Ms. Osborne worked as a law clerk at Osborne Law Offices, P.C. representing the interests of labor unions and individual employees. During law school, Ms. Osborne worked as the legal intern for the Pittsburgh Pirates where she assisted In-House Counsel review contracts for stadium events and team support, front office operations, and day-to-day baseball operations. Additionally, Ms. Osborne worked as an intern in The House of Representatives for Congressman Tim Ryan and his legislative staff where she helped perform research for the introduction of Bills to the House floor.

Prior to her legal training, Ms. Osborne obtained her undergraduate degree from The University of Scranton where she majored in Criminal Justice with a concentration in Women’s Studies. While attending the University of Scranton, Ms. Osborne became a founding member of Scranton’s first Mock Trial Team. Ms. Osborne is licensed to practice law in the District of Columbia and before federal agencies nationwide.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning - Trusts Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Real estate, estate planning, and business law are the focal points of Michael J. Overson’s law practice. As a member of the Real Estate Section of the Virginia State Bar, Mr. Overson has experience representing clients in a wide variety of real estate matters, including purchases, sales, easements, leases, boundary line adjustments, and related litigation. A substantial part of Mr. Overson’s practice involves the representation of landlords and tenants in eviction proceedings and other lease disputes.

In addition to his real estate practice, Mr. Overson advises clients on estate planning and taxation issues, and regularly assists clients in the preparation of wills, trusts, and other estate planning documents. Mr. Overson also advises clients on business law and organizational matters, and has assisted numerous clients in the formation of limited liability companies and other Virginia business entities.

Prior to joining Moyes Hanssen Overson, PLLC in 2012, Mr. Overson practiced real estate law in Boston, Massachusetts for five years. He graduated from Suffolk University Law School in 2006, and from Boston College in 2003. He currently lives in Leesburg, Virginia with his wife and daughter.

attorneys.name: Michael Thomas Pallai
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
With over 15 years of experience, Michael “Mike” Pallai is a skilled advocate for those who are navigating some of life’s most challenging circumstances. Equally comfortable behind his desk or in front of a judge, Mr. Pallai’s practice is broad and varied, but he has developed a particular specialization in the areas of workers’ compensation, personal injury, family law and criminal defense. Whether it is ensuring injured workers receive the benefits and medical care they are entitled to, negotiating with automobile insurance companies so victims of negligence receive a just settlement, or protecting client’s rights in family law matters or a criminal courtroom, Mr. Pallai is client-focused and works tirelessly to achieve the best outcomes for his clients.

With years of hands-on experience both in and out of the courtroom, Mr. Pallai takes a practical, down-to-earth approach to every case and clients appreciate his candor. He works closely with them to understand their needs, explain their rights, and create a plan that gets results — whether that means negotiating a fair settlement or taking a case to trial. Clients can expect honest answers, clear advice, and strong legal support every step of the way.

attorneys.name: Anthony Paone II
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Tony concentrates his practice primarily in family law and divorce; real estate litigation and general civil litigation and probate matters. He has been practicing law thirty years in central Virginia, and was the founder of his own firm which he ran successfully for over twenty years.

He is an experienced litigator, with a priority focused on meeting his clients' goals, whether in the court room or through negotiation and mediation. He understands that while experience affords him the knowledge to recognize similarities and overlaps in cases that he has handled, he knows that each case is unique and that sometimes a rare set of facts and legal issues presents itself that requires special effort and a dedicated strategy to resolve. Often this requires flexibility and the need to change gears at a moment's notice.

He is a past President of the Goochland County Bar Association. Tony has served his community through civic involvement in several organizations, including positions on the local Board of Directors for Goochland CASA and the local chapter of the American Red Cross for Goochland County, as well as coaching baseball and time as a Scouting leader.

attorneys.name: Joseph T. Patton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in McLean, VA
attorneys.bio:
Joseph’s practice has focused exclusively on a full range of family law matters, including divorce, custody, child and spousal support, property division, premarital, marital, and separation agreements, and protective orders. He has extensive trial experience, but also adheres to the belief that families are generally better served - and his counsel is particularly effective - when disputes are resolved outside the courtroom.

Joseph is originally from Pittsburgh and earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Economics from the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School. He later received his Juris Doctor degree from George Mason University Law School. While in law school, he participated in the Domestic Relations Legal Clinic, providing legal services to clients in uncontested divorces, and was president of the Black Law Students Association.
