Joseph is a member of the Virginia State Bar and the Fairfax Bar Association and has appeared in courts throughout Northern Virginia, including Alexandria, Arlington, Clarke, Fairfax, Frederick, King George, Loudoun, Prince William, Spotsylvania, Stafford, and Winchester.

attorneys.name: Abigail Paules
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Abigail Paules is an attorney who has spent her legal career being a zealous advocate for her clients and defending their rights under the Constitution.

Abigail received her Bachelor of Arts degree from Bucknell University where she majored in history and political science. She received her law degree from William and Mary Law School.

She began her legal career at the Office of the Public Defender for the City of Richmond. She spent almost six years at the Richmond Public Defender's Office, earning the title of Senior Assistant Public Defender. She spent her time at the public defender's office representing indigent clients charged with all types of crimes. As a Senior Assistant Public Defender in Richmond, Abigail handled close to two thousand cases, including all types of misdemeanors and felonies, such as first degree murder, armed robbery, felonious assault, and nearly everything in between. She has tried numerous cases, both bench and jury trials, argued complex motions, and had contested sentencings in general district court, juvenile and domestic relations court, and circuit court.

She handles all types of criminal cases in numerous jurisdictions throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia. Abigail is a firm proponent of the Sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution; and she believes in the right to the effective assistance of counsel, no matter one's income or background.

attorneys.name: Paul R. Pearson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Rated AV Preeminent® by Martindale-Hubble

Paul Pearson has an extensive background in civil litigation in state and federal courts in Virginia, Maryland, and the District of Columbia. His focus includes cases involving products liability, personal injury, automobile accidents, false arrest, malicious prosecution, construction and contract litigation, and other commercial disputes.

Mr. Pearson began with the firm of Arthur & Speed in 1979, eventually becoming a partner in the firm known as Arthur, Pearson and Martin. Paul represented clients who had been injured as the result of someone else’s negligence. During this time, Paul tried more than 100 cases in state and federal courts in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia. During his career, Mr. Pearson has handled numerous cases of catastrophic injury, including wrongful death and traumatic brain injury.

Paul was also "designated counsel" for Borg-Warner Security Corporation, an international company with divisions including private security, courier, armored car service, and fire and burglar alarm services.

After 22 years in private practice, Paul joined the Travelers Staff Counsel Office in October 2001, where he was specifically responsible for handling all major cases. He was subsequently appointed as Practice Group Leader, overseeing and mentoring the liability lawyers in all of Virginia, while continuing to handle his own cases.

After retiring from Travelers in March 2018, Paul joined Weiner, Spivey & Miller in September 2018, where he once again represents personal injury clients as he did in earlier private practice. Paul employs his 44 years of unique practice experience, gained from representing both plaintiffs and defendants, to provide a balanced evaluation and approach to obtaining the best possible result for injured clients.

A native of Montgomery County, Maryland, Paul served in the United States Army Special Forces Reserve (11th Special Forces Group, Airborne) from 1966 to 1973. Paul and his wife celebrated their 50th anniversary in 2022. They have four adult children, four grandchildren, and two great granchildren.

When he’s not working, he enjoys spending time with his family and horseback riding. Paul is active with the Hunters Valley Association and Hunters Valley Riding Club.

attorneys.name: Bryan S. Peeples
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain / Right of Way Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Bryan focuses his practice in the areas of maritime and riparian law, construction law, worker's compensation, and national security. A prolific author, Bryan has written articles on Virginia aquaculture and maritime law, including the Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act; the Virginia Primary Sand Dune and Beaches Act; and the Virginia Tidal Wetlands Act. He has been published in a number of professional journals on a variety of topics, ranging from Virginia real property law to the Anti-Terrorism Act.

Bryan is a member of the firm's waterfront law practice group, and writes blog articles regularly on the group's website devoted to waterfront (riparian) property rights law, maritime and admiralty law, and environmental law. Please click here to visit the waterfront law team's website.

Before joining the firm is 2018, Bryan retired from the U.S. Navy after 22 years of service as a pilot. He completed seven combat deployments and served as the Commanding Officer of a helicopter squadron. His last assignment was Lead Rotational Planner for the Joint Staff, where he provided strategic advice to the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs and the Secretary of Defense.

attorneys.bio:
Blake Pendleton is an associate in Odin Feldman Pittleman’s Litigation Practice Group, where he draws on his judicial clerkship and litigation experience to advocate for clients in complex disputes.

Before joining the firm, Blake served as an Administrative Law Clerk to the Honorable Daniel E. Ortiz of the Court of Appeals of Virginia, where he drafted published and unpublished opinions in a wide range of civil and criminal appeals and prepared bench memoranda for pre-panel review. He also clerked for the Honorable Michael E. Levy, Victoria A.B. Willis, and J. Bruce Strickland of the Stafford County Circuit Court, assisting with complex motions, election recounts, probation violation petitions, and a high volume of domestic and uncontested matters.

Blake’s prior experience includes work with the U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division, Criminal Section, where he supported federal hate crimes prosecutions, and with the George Mason Veterans and Servicemembers Legal Clinic, where he advised servicemembers and veterans on family law and benefits issues. He also gained judicial experience as a Judicial Intern to the Honorable Thomas T. Cullen of the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Virginia and as a legal intern with the Fairfax Office of the Public Defender. In addition, Blake clerked with Sher, Cummings & Ellis in Arlington, supporting complex securities litigation.

Blake earned his J.D. from the George Mason School of Law and brings a detail-oriented, analytical approach to each matter he handles.

attorneys.name: Jonathan Monroe Petty
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan's law practice focuses on litigation, predominantly in the representation of the victims of serious personal injury or death. Prior to co-founding Petty & Mullen PC, Jonathan was a partner at LeClair Ryan, one of the largest law firms in Virginia, where he was a member of the medical malpractice and products liability defense trial team. He has successfully tried personal injury cases to verdict in courts throughout the Commonwealth, from Richmond to Tidewater to Northern Virginia. Jonathan is licensed to practice law in both Virginia and Georgia, and he has handled cases on behalf of both plaintiffs and defendants in State and Federal Courts across the country.

Beginning in 1994, Jonathan became involved in representing doctors, hospitals and insurance companies involved in complex medical malpractice litigation, including cases involving surgical errors, failure to diagnose cancer, cardiac death and birth-related injuries. Earlier in his career, he also represented large corporations in defending wrongful death and catastrophic injury cases involving tractor-trailer accidents and defective products. As a former defense lawyer, Jonathan gained valuable insight into how these complicated cases are defended. Since leaving the defense bar, he has applied this knowledge and experience exclusively to representing individuals who have suffered injuries and damages caused by the negligence and carelessness of others such as doctors, hospitals, careless drivers, product manufacturers, and others.

Jonathan chairs the personal injury practice at Petty & Mullen PC. He is a member of The Association of the Trial Lawyers of America, the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association and the Richmond Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Susan F. Pierce
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Warrenton, VA
attorneys.bio:
Susan F. Pierce is a tireless advocate for individuals injured in car, motorcycle, and trucking accidents. With over thirty years of personal injury experience, she is keenly aware that all injuries, and all cases, are unique.

An injury impacts many aspects of a client’s life, as well as their family members. A client may lose their job, become overburdened with medical and other bills, and forego treatment due to injuries and financial issues. Susan works to obtain the maximum recovery to compensate her clients for their physical, mental, and financial injuries.

Susan focuses on serious personal injury cases including fatalities from car or trucking accidents, brain or other traumatic injuries, and victims of assault and drunk driving.

When she is not in the office, Susan likes to read and write fiction, and travel with her family.

attorneys.name: Scott W. Pohlman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Business Planning Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Scott W. Pohlman, a member partner in Hale Carlson Baumgartner, PLC, practices in the areas of Commercial and Business Law, Franchise Law and Wealth Preservation (Estate Planning). He represents businesses, business owners and individuals in Virginia, Pennsylvania and New York and is licensed to practice in all three states. Prior to joining Hale Carlson Baumgartner, PLC he was a partner in Baumgartner Pohlman, PLC. Before returning to private practice in Virginia he served as General Counsel for a large Washington DC-based commercial sub-contractor. He previously practiced law in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.

Mr. Pohlman serves on the board of LawPact (www.LawPact.org), an international association and network of independent business law firms created to assist member firms in pursuing excellence in: client service, firm management, profitability, the application of evolving technologies and marketing and establishing a trans-national source of known legal colleagues to serve the global legal needs of member firm clients.

Mr. Pohlman has represented a variety of clients during all stages of business development, both start-ups and established businesses. He has guided and worked with companies who have been selected to INC Magazine's Fastest Growing 500 list. Mr. Pohlman has expertise in assisting companies through the acquisition and sale process. His representation includes privately held companies, as well as publicly traded international businesses.

Mr. Pohlman represents a wide variety of businesses, in the following industries: communications, broadcasting, trade associations, construction, medical service providers, non-profits (both charitable and educational), consulting, foodservice, financial services, franchises, equipment rental providers, agriculture and many others. His clients often include businesses with varied ownership structures (single-member or owner organizations; multiple owner organizations and family-owned companies that have successfully transitioned from the founding generation to successive generations of family owners). In addition to his legal experience and expertise, Mr. Pohlman has personally managed large-scale construction projects in the United States and abroad and has worked in and for several family-owned businesses.

In addition to his business entity representation, Mr. Pohlman represents business executives on a personal level, providing guidance and counseling related to their contracting and employment needs, including personal estate planning needs.

He has guided and worked with companies who have been selected to INC Magazine's Fastest Growing 500 list. Mr. Pohlman has expertise in assisting companies through the acquisition and sale process. His representation includes privately held companies, as well as publicly traded international businesses.

Mr. Pohlman represents a wide variety of businesses, in the following industries: communications, broadcasting, trade associations, construction, medical service providers, non-profits (both charitable and educational), consulting, foodservice, financial services, franchises, equipment rental providers, agriculture and many others. His clients often include businesses with varied ownership structures (single-member or owner organizations; multiple owner organizations and family-owned companies that have successfully transitioned from the founding generation to successive generations of family owners). Additionally, Danielle's comment on the proposed International Megan's Law of 2010 was published in Fall 2011.

Danielle studied psychology at the University of Virginia. She is a native of Miami, Florida but has called Virginia home since 1998.

attorneys.name: Sonya L. Powell
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Powell has been practicing solely in the area of family law since 1994. By limiting her practice exclusively to family law, she has become well versed and knowledgeable in all aspects of domestic relations litigation. Ms. Powell has litigated or settled cases involving complex issues of equitable distribution including tracing of separate property interests, valuation of businesses, retirement issues, and significant financial investments and portfolios. Ms. Powell has represented clients in alimony and child support cases on all income levels. She has had substantial courtroom experience in successfully defending against, and advocating for, imputation of income to a party for support purposes and deviations from child support guidelines for such factors as a child's special needs or private school costs. She also has litigated or settled child custody cases, involving diverse issues such as the admissibility of expert testimony of custody evaluators, substance abuse issues, domestic violence and relocation of a parent. Ms. Powell recognizes the emotional and financial benefits to her clients of resolving cases, if possible, without the necessity of going to court. Her primary goal is to settle cases through the negotiation process, which can include mediation, whenever possible. However, she is confident in her trial skills if her cases end up in court. Through the course of her representation, Ms. Powell's clients can be assured that she will be a strong, knowledgeable and well-prepared advocate for their interests.

Ms. Powell receives a preeminent rating (AV) from the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory and has been listed in the treatise The Best Lawyers in America since 2012. Ms. Powell is recognized as one of Virginia's Super Lawyers and one of the top 100 Super Lawyers in Virginia and top 50 women attorneys in Virginia. She was included in The Washingtonian magazine as one of Northern Virginia's top family law practitioners since 2018 and listed as a top divorce lawyer by Northern Virginia Magazine.

Ms. Powell serves on the Board of Directors for the Falls Church-Mclean Children's Center, a non-profit organization dedicated to providing early education to all children, regardless of socioeconomic status. She is also a member of the Hispanic Bar Association of Virginia and Fairfax Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Kabara Korth Praskavich
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Falls Church, VA
attorneys.bio:
Kabara Korth Praskavich is a partner with Maddox & Gerock. Kabara has focused her entire career on domestic relations and works to ensure her clients understand the process, the goal, and the strategy, during a time that can often feel overwhelming or daunting. Kabara has experience leading clients through all types of family law cases including custody, support, property, and enforcement issues. She is especially well versed and interested in cases that involve complex financial analysis including business valuations, executive compensation, and waste analysis, and she is sought as a national speaker on these topics.

Kabara's strategy is tailored to each specific case – some are able to resolve amicably with simple negotiation or mediation, others may require extensive litigation and the use of numerous experts – most cases fall somewhere in the middle. Which approach is right will depend on the client’s goals, the costs of achieving those goals (emotional and financial), and the facts presented in each unique case.

Kabara moved to the DC area to attend law school at Georgetown Law, where she received the pro bono certificate for completing over 350 hours of volunteer legal services – almost exclusively in the area of domestic relations. While at Georgetown, Kabara interned at Servicemembers Legal Defense Network (SLDN), working with LGBT and HIV-positive service members facing court martial and discharge under the former policy of “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell,” and clerked in the DC Superior Court, gaining experience on issues of adoption, civil commitment, and cases involving CPS.

Prior to law school, Kabara graduated from the University of Chicago where she received a degree in history. Kabara currently lives in Maryland with her spouse, children, and dog. When not in the office, Kabara enjoys traveling, reading, hiking, and all things nerdy.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Kabara Korth Praskavich is a partner with Maddox & Gerock. Kabara has focused her entire career on domestic relations and works to ensure her clients understand the process, the goal, and the strategy, during a time that can often feel overwhelming or daunting. Kabara has experience leading clients through all types of family law cases including custody, support, property, and enforcement issues. She is especially well versed and interested in cases that involve complex financial analysis including business valuations, executive compensation, and waste analysis, and she is sought as a national speaker on these topics.

Kabara's strategy is tailored to each specific case – some are able to resolve amicably with simple negotiation or mediation, others may require extensive litigation and the use of numerous experts – most cases fall somewhere in the middle. Which approach is right will depend on the client’s goals, the costs of achieving those goals (emotional and financial), and the facts presented in each unique case.

Kabara moved to the DC area to attend law school at Georgetown Law, where she received the pro bono certificate for completing over 350 hours of volunteer legal services – almost exclusively in the area of domestic relations. While at Georgetown, Kabara interned at Servicemembers Legal Defense Network (SLDN), working with LGBT and HIV-positive service members facing court martial and discharge under the former policy of “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell,” and clerked in the DC Superior Court, gaining experience on issues of adoption, civil commitment, and cases involving CPS.

Prior to law school, Kabara graduated from the University of Chicago where she received a degree in history. Kabara currently lives in Maryland with her spouse, children, and dog. When not in the office, Kabara enjoys traveling, reading, hiking, and all things nerdy.

attorneys.name: Joy Lee Price
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Lynchburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from law school in 1989, Joy Lee Price returned to Lynchburg, where she has practiced law for over 25 years. Her primary focus is on civil litigation, with a particular emphasis on divorce, child custody, and other family law related matters. She is admitted to practice in all federal and state courts in Virginia.

Joy Lee is a graduate of the University of Tennessee, where she received a B.S. with high honors. She earned her law degree from the Marshall-Wythe School of Law at the College of William & Mary.

Joy Lee is a member of the Fourth Circuit Judicial Conference, and she is a past President of both the Lynchburg Bar Association and the Family Law Section of the Lynchburg Bar. She currently serves on the Boards of Directors of the Lynchburg Humane Society, Mental Health America of Central Virginia, and Miriam’s House.

attorneys.name: John K. Prillaman
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Roanoke, VA
attorneys.bio:
John Prillaman concentrates his legal practice in (i) corporate and business law for closely held businesses and (ii) estate planning and trusts and estates administration, which often involves taxation and business planning and related transactions. John handles a wide range of corporate and business matters for business owners from entity formation to governance and dissolution, including contract drafting and negotiation, real estate purchase and sales, dispute resolution, and litigation. John also represents several banks and credit unions on general corporate governance, bankruptcy and collection matters, and has an active Landlord/Tenant and Adoption practice. John was recognized by Virginia Super Lawyers as a Rising Star in 2013.

John is a Roanoke native and moved back to Roanoke in 2010. Prior to joining OPN Law, John was an associate at Woods Rogers, PLC and the General Counsel for the Roanoke Redevelopment and Housing Authority.

John enjoys spending his free time with his wife, family, and friends engaging in a wide range of outdoor and personal activities including soccer, golf, guitar, and fishing. John is actively involved in Second Presbyterian Church and serves on the North Cross Alumni Board.

attorneys.name: Michael T. Pritchard
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Michael Pritchard has represented individuals and business before many state and federal courts and administrative agencies on Title VII, ADA, ADEA, FMLA, ERISA, and other employment cases. In addition to litigation of employment matters, Mr. Pritchard also advises employers on compliance with federal and state employment laws, employment policies and handbooks, non-compete agreements, handling internal investigations of discrimination and harassment and best practices for a variety of other human resource issues.

With a background in labor and employment law, Mr. Pritchard’s practice quickly spread to other areas of civil and criminal litigation. Mr. Pritchard has tried cases in state and federal court ranging from civil cases involving contract disputes, fraud, construction law, real estate, and consumer protection to criminal cases involving larceny, identity theft, government contract fraud, conspiracy, bribery and other white collar crimes.

Mr. Pritchard’s criminal practice includes extensive work handling drug offenses, DUI/DWI and other traffic offenses. He also has experience with juvenile cases both in the Juvenile & Domestic Relations Courts and in school board expulsion/disciplinary hearings.

attorneys.name: Ryan Probasco
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Probasco was born and raised in Arlington, Virginia. He received his B.A. Degree in Political Science and History, with honors, from Virginia Tech. Ryan attended American University Washington College of Law beginning in 2010, was a member of the American University Law Review, and graduated with honors. While in law school, Ryan began interning as a law clerk for Pikrallidas & Associates in the summer of 2011, and joined the firm as an associate upon passing the Virginia bar exam in October of 2013. After successfully litigating and trying an innumerable number of cases in personal injury, commercial litigation, landlord-tenant disputes, and criminal defense, he became a partner in the firm.

At Pikrallidas & Probasco, Ryan’s practice is focused on civil litigation, with an emphasis on personal injury and commercial litigation. He regularly represents plaintiffs in Virginia, Maryland, and the District of Columbia seeking to recover for their injuries resulting from car accidents, falling merchandise, and the negligent maintenance of premises. He has experience trying cases all over the state of Virginia, including in its federal courts.

Besides his civil practice, Ryan also routinely represents people facing criminal charges. Ryan has experience litigating a wide range of misdemeanor and felony cases and routinely represents persons accused of driving while intoxicated or reckless driving in courts throughout Virginia.

Ryan is a member of the Virginia Bar Association, Fairfax Bar Association, and the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association. Ryan is licensed to practice law in Virginia, Maryland, the District of Columbia, and California. Ryan is also licensed to appear before the United States Court for the Eastern and Western Districts of Virginia. Ryan truly enjoys working closely with clients and tries his best to zealously represent his clients’ interests to the fullest extent possible.

In his free time, Ryan enjoys spending time with his wife and son, playing tennis, lifting weights, and debating the law with anyone who will listen.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office Of Joan H. Proper, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Special Education Law in the public school system (Infant and Toddler through High School) Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Joan Heishman Proper represents clients in education and Guardianship and Conservatorship matters.

Ms. Proper’s education practice is focused on special education and general education matters in the public school system (preschool through high school) including bullying issues, student discipline, student behavior, student attendance, IEP and 504 issues, and other matters.

Although Ms. Proper has almost eighteen years of family law practice, she is focusing on education and guardianship and conservatorship matters. She is no longer taking new family law cases.

Prior to law school, Ms. Proper was a teacher for nine years, first in the Diocese of Arlington and then in Fairfax County Public Schools. While she was a general education teacher, she taught students with a wide variety of special education needs.

In addition to her other areas of practice, Ms. Proper is also certified as a Guardian ad litem for children and incapacitated adults in guardianship, conservatorship and family law matters.

attorneys.practice_type: Mergers and acquisitions structures and strategies Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Tom is a Shareholder of Odin Feldman Pittleman and has been practicing for nearly 25 years. Tom believes that his accessibility, responsiveness, and common-sense practical solutions are the keys to his building successful relationships with his clients. He also believes that his background as a former CPA differentiates him from other lawyers and helps him better understand his clients' businesses, goals and problems so that he can deliver cost-effective, practical advice to them.

Tom focuses his practice on mergers and acquisitions, entity formation, governance, and succession planning, tax and business planning, and reviewing commercial contracts. He advises established and early-stage companies in a wide range of business transactions and has particular experience working on transactions in the healthcare, professional services, government contracting, information technology, and construction industries.

Tom lives in Leesburg, Virginia, with his wife and five children. When not working, he can be found on the lacrosse fields of Loudoun County watching his children play.

attorneys.name: Cynthia M. Radomsky
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Radomsky's approach to the practice of family law is client-centered. In other words, her goals are to make you feel comfortable and cared for as a person as well as to provide you with top notch legal advice and legal representation.

Most of Ms. Radomsky's cases settle favorably out of court, which is the best outcome because it allows you to remain in control of how you will parent your children and how you will divide your assets and debts rather than allowing a judge to decide based on the limited information that is admissible in court. Settlement also keeps your attorney fees down and reduces the likelihood of future litigation.

Ms. Radomsky has completed the training necessary to practice collaborative law, which is a fairly new process that allows the parties to agree to stay out of the court system to resolve their marital problems privately while still within a formal structure. In a collaborative divorce, each party has an attorney, and often the parties share a team of neutral experts in the areas that apply to their case - like finance, mental health, and parenting - to make well educated decisions about their future. To have a collaborative divorce, both parties must agree to participate in the process, to disclose all relevant information, and to retain an attorney with the required training. If your spouse is not represented by a collaborative attorney, settlement is still possible through mediation or through more traditional negotiation.

If you and your spouse choose to resolve your marital problems through the process of mediation, your mediator will be a neutral who cannot provide you with legal advice or protect your individual interests. Ms. Radomsky can represent you by guiding you through the mediation process and making sure you understand the law and make sound decisions. In the alternative, Ms. Radomsky is able to serve in the role of the neutral mediator.

If a fair settlement is not possible, Ms. Radomsky is prepared to advocate for you to the judge. Since 2006, she has handled an array of family law cases in Virginia trial courts, ranging from complex divorce cases involving business valuations to more discrete post-divorce motions to modify or enforce prior custody, visitation, and support awards.

Ms. Radomsky has been recognized in the Washingtonian and Northern Virginia Magazine as one of the area's top family law attorneys. Ms. Radomsky has been recognized as a Virginia Super Lawyer since 2013, which is based on peer nominations, peer evaluations, and independent research. She has also been included in the Super Lawyer list of the Top 50 Women Lawyers in Virginia and the list of the Top 100 Lawyers in Virginia. Throughout her career, Ms. Radomsky has been active in the area of Continuing Legal Education. She was selected by the Virginia Supreme Court as a member of the Mandatory Continuing Legal Education Board from 2014-2017; and, she has been a member of the Fairfax Bar Association’s Continuing Legal Education Committee since 2006, serving as a the Committee co-chair in 2011-2013 and vice chair in 2010. She has spoken as a panelist on the topic of family law at the 2016 Fall Conference & 35th Anniversary Celebration of the Virginia Women Attorneys Association and at a 2012 seminar presented by the Virginia Pro Bono Law Center. She received her training certificate from the Collaborative Practice Training Institute in 2018 and is a member of the International Academy of Collaborative Professionals, Collaborative Professionals of Northern Virginia, and Virginia Collaborative Professionals. Ms. Radomsky completed 40 hours of mediation and interest-based negotiation skills training in September of 2020. Ms. Radomsky is a member of the family law sections of the Virginia State Bar, the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, and the Fairfax Bar Association. She is also a member of the Arlington Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Meena H. Rajan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Meena Rajan has been a practicing attorney since 2011 and has been focused primarily on family law since 2012. She has handled complicated relocations cases, contested custody issues, spousal support battles and complex equitable distribution cases. In addition, she has experience with criminal defense and understands the interplay between family law and criminal-adjacent issues, including Protective Orders. She has appeared in courts in Fairfax, Loudoun, Prince William, Alexandria and Arlington counties.

Meena loves working with clients and helping them navigate difficult situations and reach a resolution that is best for them and their family. Meena understands that there is no one size fits all in family law. She is cognizant that a protracted legal battle is often not the best thing for clients but is always willing to litigate when the situation warrants it. She takes a practical approach to her cases and works hard to develop strong relationships with her clients.

Meena graduated cum laude from George Mason University School of Law in 2011. She is admitted to the Virginia Bar, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia and the District of Columbia Bar. Prior to attending law school, Meena worked in the Human Resources field for over five years. While she grew up in New York and Connecticut, she is a 20+ year resident of Fairfax County.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Rambudhan is a dual practice attorney who specializes in Family Law and Criminal Litigation.

Criminal/Traffic

Having previously worked for a prosecutor's office in New York, Mr. Rambudhan brings a unique set of skills to the firm. He understands how police and prosecutors approach cases, and uses that knowledge to build a strategic defense for his clients who face criminal charges. Mr. Rambudhan believes in a three-step approach to accomplishing a solid defense: (1) diligent preparation and research; (2) effective and aggressive negotiations; and (3) desire and confidence to litigate any case if necessary.

Family Law

Having previously worked with one of the best family attorneys in Fairfax, Mr. Rambudhan witnessed first hand how important it is that people have a terrific lawyer to represent them in divorce, custody, or child-support disputes. He is a passionate and aggressive advocate for his clients and works tirelessly to defend their rights and protect their loved ones.

attorneys.practice_type: Ethics & Professional Responsibility Lawyers in Alexandria, VA
attorneys.bio:
McGavock Reed is an experienced attorney with an extensive background in attorney ethics and bar discipline matters. Having dedicated his career to this specialized practice area, he brings a wealth of experience and knowledge to the field. McGavock’s expertise in attorney ethics is unmatched, making him a trusted and sought-after advisor for lawyers in Washington D.C. and Virginia.

Throughout his career, McGavock has successfully defended attorneys across various practice areas, including immigration law, family law, criminal defense, patent law, civil litigation, probate law, veterans law, and in-house counsel. His deep understanding of the disciplinary process and his ability to navigate complex legal issues with precision and skill have earned him a stellar reputation among his peers.

In addition to his prowess in attorney ethics, McGavock is also well-versed in business law, providing strategic counsel to clients on matters such as business contracts, operating agreements, formation, dissolution, and litigation. His meticulous attention to detail and ability to find innovative solutions make him a valuable asset to businesses of all sizes.

McGavock’s academic achievements and professional affiliations further highlight his dedication to the legal profession. He obtained his JD from Catholic University Columbus School of Law, and while in school was the Executive Editor of the Journal of Contemporary Health Law and Policy, Vice Chancellor of the Moot Court Association, instructor for the Street Law Program and a competing member of the Society of Trial Advocates.

Recognized for his exceptional track record and outstanding legal acumen, McGavock is affiliated with prestigious organizations such as the DC Bar, Virginia Bar, APRL, AVVO, Fairfax Bar Association, and the Alexandria Chamber of Commerce. These affiliations are a testament to his standing in the legal community and his commitment to upholding the highest ethical standards.

When you choose McGavock Reed as your legal counsel, you can rest assured that you are working with an attorney who not only understands the intricacies of attorney ethics and discipline matters but is also deeply invested in protecting your interests. attorneys.name: Duncan P. Reid
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Duncan Reid graduated from the College of William and Mary in 1970 and from the University of Richmond Law School in 1975. After being admitted to the Bar in 1975, he was in a general private practice through 1976.

In 1977, Duncan Reid started a thirty-five year career with the Henrico County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office. He served as the Chief Deputy the last eighteen of those years. While at the Commonwealth’s Attorney’s office, he tried hundreds of jury trials, including multiple capital murder trials, the Piper Rountree case and the first case in Henrico involving DNA. Duncan Reid was the lead prosecutor in one of the Nation’s first cases using a Geographic Information System to enhance a fingerprint from a crime scene and also tried one of the first cases in Virginia using cell towers to prove a murder.

Since retiring from public service in 2011, Duncan Reid has used his wealth of experience to represent clients facing criminal and traffic charges and assist in the firm's civil practice.

attorneys.name: Tenecia Reid
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Tenecia P. Reid brings more than two decades of experience and a proven record of zealous advocacy in family law to our firm, where she is dedicated to guiding her clients through their most challenging domestic matters.

Admitted to the California State Bar in 2003, Ms. Reid began her career at a Los Angeles law firm before establishing and successfully managing her own family law practice. After relocating to Loudoun County, Virginia, she was admitted to the Virginia State Bar in 2009 and has since built a reputation as a trusted advocate in divorce, custody, and other domestic relations matters. For more than a decade, she served clients across Northern Virginia through her own firm, honing her skills in both complex litigation and negotiated resolutions.

Ms. Reid is adept at handling the full spectrum of family law cases, from straightforward uncontested divorces to high-stakes disputes involving significant assets and emotionally charged custody issues. She understands that each matter calls for a tailored approach, whether calm and pragmatic or assertive and decisive.

Residing in Loudoun County with her two children and their Goldendoodle, Hazel Jane, Ms. Reid enjoys reading, traveling, and is an active member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Glen Allen, VA
attorneys.bio:
At the law firm of Jacqueline M. Reiner, PLLC, clients benefit from the experience, skill and tenacity of a seasoned trial lawyer. Jacqueline Reiner, a former prosecutor for the City for Richmond brings a persistent, aggressive and personalized style to the practice of criminal defense, and protective order litigation.

Every attorney-client relationship with Ms. Reiner is founded upon clear and regular communication and trust. Criminal defense and protective order litigation clients play an active role in strategizing and achieving desired outcomes. Realistic and practical advice, hard work, compassion and integrity are essential ingredients in all client representations. Ms. Reiner recognizes that an effective legal strategy is oftentimes akin to a strong business strategy. Previous corporate firm experience gives her the ability to offer practical, goal-oriented, cost-effective representation on legal matters including DUI and criminal cases. Costs, risks and projected benefits merit careful consideration and analysis whether your case involves protective order litigation; a juvenile or young adult seeking to keep a clean record following an arrest for underage drinking, drug use or shoplifting; domestic or other violent crimes; drug or property offenses.

Ms. Reiner knows the value of experience, preparation and trial readiness and her clients benefit from the same. Prosecutors and other legal opponents know that Jacqueline Reiner will bring your case to a judge or jury when necessary. Ms. Reiner’s regular appearances in the criminal and civil courts throughout central Virginia keep her skills sharp and relationships solid within the legal community. All these factors contribute to the strong, personalized, results-oriented advocacy Ms. Reiner’s clients receive.

Jacqueline M. Reiner, PLLC welcomes inquiries from persons seeking representation in Virginia in criminal, protective order litigation, and other legal matters.

attorneys.name: Nicholas David Renninger
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations/Family Law Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Nick Renninger and his family have called the Tidewater area of Virginia home since 2002, after moving here from Vermont. Nick earned his J.D. from Regent University School of Law in Virginia Beach, VA, where he graduated in the top third of his class. While attending Regent University, Nick was on the Dean's List and held leadership positions in Student Government and the Regent Journal of International Law, where he served as a Managing Editor. He was also the recipient of the Academic Merit Award and Dean's Scholarship.

Before entering private practice, Nick was an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney for the City of Suffolk where he prosecuted white collar and general property crimes as well as domestic violence crimes. During law school, Nick clerked for the Honorable William R. Savage, III, of the Suffolk General District and Circuit Courts, and also interned for the Suffolk Commonwealth's Attorney's Office.

Nick devotes his practice to representing clients in difficult family law related matters, as well as serious criminal matters in state and federal courts. Nick also serves as Guardian ad Litem for minor children in custody disputes.

In his spare time, Nick is active in his community and enjoys running, playing tennis, and spending time with his wife and son.

attorneys.bio:
Ida is an English and Farsi-speaking Iranian-American born and raised in Northern Virginia.

She graduated from Radford University, summa cum laude, with a degree in Criminal Justice in 2018. She attended the West Virginia University College of Law and graduated with a Juris Doctor degree in 2021. While in law school, Ida was a member of the Family Law Quarterly Journal. She also worked as a student attorney in the West Virginia Innocence Project Clinic and helped draft a writ of certiorari to the Supreme Court of the United States.

Richardson, Ill advises and represents clients in all aspects of commercial and business practice, including both commercial transactions and litigation, with an emphasis on construction, design liability, property transactions, commercial disputes, and labor/employment law. attorneys.name: Leslie Sue Ritts
attorneys.practice_type: Toxic tort/general environmental litigation Lawyers in Alexandria, VA
attorneys.bio:
Leslie Ritts' practice includes representation of clients before the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, other federal, state, and local natural resource agencies, and before the federal and state courts. Since the early 1980s, she has been involved in many significant environmental rulemakings, most prominently affecting Clean Air Act permitting approvals and control requirements for new and existing industrial sources. This regulatory background especially qualifies Leslie to advise clients on pro-active strategies for obtaining environmental permits and complying with environmental regulations. In addition, her prominent role in advising clients on development and compliance with Clean Air Act regulations has led to her defense of several multinational companies in Clean Air Act NSR and multi-media enforcement actions. Leslie also represents several national associations challenging U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) final regulations in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia.

Leslie also has represented private and governmental entities on a wide variety of other environmental and transactional issues, including Superfund clean-ups and Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA)-natural resource claims, as well as compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act Section 404 program, the Endangered Species Act, and Coastal Barrier Resources Act. She also has represented clients involved in personal injury suits and class actions arising from alleged exposures to hazardous substances.

A registered lobbyist, Leslie has been heavily involved in legislative activities in U.S. Congress affecting core environmental laws over the last two decades. In addition to several national manufacturing trade associations she advises, she served as Chairman of the Air & Waste Management Association's (AWMA) Government Affairs Committee from 1993-1996 advising AWMA on public policy issues affecting the 17,000 member professional association.

Leslie is the author or co-author of many articles on environmental topics. She also speaks regularly at national legal and environmental professional conferences on environmental law issues.

Albemarle County native, Kelly Roberts, joined the firm in 2015. She spent the first eight years of her practice in the Hampton Roads, Virginia area practicing civil litigation, with an emphasis in family law. In times of chaos, Ms. Roberts’ sympathetic ear has brought comfort to many clients. Do not let her kind demeanor fool you – she knows when to be aggressive. Mrs. Roberts represents clients in a wide area of contested civil litigation across eighteen venues. Mrs. Roberts travels between our Staunton, Harrisonburg and Charlottesville offices, and is able to meet with clients in any of our four (4) office locations.

Mrs. Roberts had the honor of serving as Staff Attorney with the Legal Aid Society of Eastern Virginia’s Tidewater Office from 2008 until 2014, when she moved back to Albemarle County where Mrs. Roberts resides with her Husband and two children. Mrs. Roberts is guided daily by her Christian faith.

attorneys.name: Brien A. Roche
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mclean, VA
attorneys.bio:
Brien A. Roche practices in the areas of personal injury, wrongful death, medical malpractice, products liability, motor vehicle accidents, workers' compensation, as well as a broad range of civil litigation. He has been an attorney since 1976. Mr. Roche is admitted to practice in Virginia, the District of Columbia, Maryland. Before working for plaintiffs in injury cases, Mr. Roche spent ten years representing insurance companies as a defendant's attorney. His experience allows him a unique insight into defense strategies and the inner workings of the insurance industry.

In addition to his busy law practice, Mr. Roche is a published author. He has written several books and articles relating to the practice of law, including the Virginia Torts Case Finder and the Virginia Domestic Relations Case Finder, two publications considered excellent reference materials used by lawyers and judges. He also wrote Law 101: An Essential Reference For Your Everyday Legal Questions, which answers many common legal questions affecting nonlawyers. Mr. Roche has also authored articles which have been published in the Journal of the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association and the Virginia Bar News.

Mr. Roche belongs to the American Bar Association, the Virginia State Bar, the District of Columbia Bar, and the Maryland State Bar. He is also a member of the Fairfax County Bar Association, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, and the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association. In 1986, Mr. Roche was appointed and continues to serve as a Commissioner in Chancery for the Circuit Court of Fairfax County, Virginia.

He earned his Juris Doctor in 1976 from George Washington University National Law Center. Mr. Roche also holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from Georgetown. From 1970-1971, Mr. Roche served as a member of the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve.

attorneys.name: Hanna Lee Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Warrenton, VA
attorneys.bio:
Hanna Lee Rodriguez While other attorneys pick an area of the law to specialize in after trying out a few different things, Hanna Lee Rodriguez likes to think that her practice area picked her.

Shortly after she joined Walker Jones, Hanna had an unexpected death in her family. Going through the probate process firsthand made her realize how essential it is to have an estate plan in place. Today, she works to help other families navigate the probate and trust administration process, mindful of the uncertainty she and her family experienced.

Hanna is passionate about working with clients who have concerns about maintaining control over their end of life care. She understands that appointing agents under financial and medical powers of attorney are very personal decisions, so a cookie-cutter approach won’t do. She thoughtfully crafts these documents and uses wills, trusts, and powers of attorney that address her client’s specific wishes and individual needs, giving them peace of mind by providing for their loved ones in the way of their own choosing.

Hanna also assists families with the process of obtaining a guardian or conservator for their loved one. Sometimes it is necessary to have the Court intervene when a person does not have an agent appointed under a medical power of attorney or general durable power of attorney. This court process can be daunting, but Hanna strives to make it as straightforward as possible. Additionally, she serves as a Guardian ad Litem for incapacitated adults in Fauquier, Rappahannock, Prince William, and Fairfax counties.

Hanna is known for her compassion and attention to detail. She is also gaining a reputation in the legal community as someone Spanish speakers can rely on for sound legal advice.

When she is not at work, Hanna enjoys spending time with her family and playing music. She is a gifted musician who plays the violin in the Piedmont Symphony Orchestra and the piano at her church.

sections.content:
Hanna Lee Rodriguez While other attorneys pick an area of the law to specialize in after trying out a few different things, Hanna Lee Rodriguez likes to think that her practice area picked her.

Shortly after she joined Walker Jones, Hanna had an unexpected death in her family. Going through the probate process firsthand made her realize how essential it is to have an estate plan in place. Today, she works to help other families navigate the probate and trust administration process, mindful of the uncertainty she and her family experienced.

Hanna is passionate about working with clients who have concerns about maintaining control over their end of life care. She understands that appointing agents under financial and medical powers of attorney are very personal decisions, so a cookie-cutter approach won’t do. She thoughtfully crafts these documents and uses wills, trusts, and powers of attorney that address her client’s specific wishes and individual needs, giving them peace of mind by providing for their loved ones in the way of their own choosing.

Hanna also assists families with the process of obtaining a guardian or conservator for their loved one. Sometimes it is necessary to have the Court intervene when a person does not have an agent appointed under a medical power of attorney or general durable power of attorney. This court process can be daunting, but Hanna strives to make it as straightforward as possible. Additionally, she serves as a Guardian ad Litem for incapacitated adults in Fauquier, Rappahannock, Prince William, and Fairfax counties.

Hanna is known for her compassion and attention to detail. She is also gaining a reputation in the legal community as someone Spanish speakers can rely on for sound legal advice.

When she is not at work, Hanna enjoys spending time with her family and playing music. She is a gifted musician who plays the violin in the Piedmont Symphony Orchestra and the piano at her church.

attorneys.name: William F. Roeder Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Lawyers in McLean, VA
attorneys.bio:
It is with a very heavy heart that we announce the passing of our friend and partner, Bud Roeder, on January 6th from complications of scleroderma induced pulmonary fibrosis. Bud was above all else, a consummate gentleman, considerate of all. His professional and pragmatic approach allowed him to be an effective advocate for his clients while retaining the respect of his opponents. Bud dedicated his life to his family, to the practice of law and to his community.

Born February 14, 1942 to William and Elizabeth Roeder, he spent the first three years of his life in Chattanooga, Tennessee where his father worked for the Tennessee Valley Authority. Raised in Falls Church, Bud graduated from George Mason High School where he was a track and field star. He was part of a 440 relay team that won the state championship title; their winning time served as a long standing record. Bud continued his track and field career at the University of the South in Sewanee, Tennessee, graduating in 1964. The next three years were spent in Charlottesville, Virginia where Bud studied law at the University of Virginia and honed an eternal appreciation for all sports Cavalier.

Upon graduation, Bud returned home to Fairfax County, beginning his long law career while serving in the Coast Guard Reserves. Cape May was a favorite posting. In private practice with a concentration on real estate and corporate finance law, Bud made a strong impact on the growth of Fairfax County. Known for his integrity, the depth of his knowledge and his mentorship of younger attorneys, Bud’s influence on the northern Virginia law community is immeasurable. He was among the founders of both the Potomac Bank and the Bank of Loudoun. Bud was proud to have served as the City Attorney for the City of Fairfax through the administrations of five Mayors.

Service to his community was an integral part of Bud’s life. He lived his faith every day in his generous actions, his kind words and his thoughtful deeds. Active in The Church of the Holy Comforter, Bud twice served as the warden of the Vestry. He cherished the Men’s Retreats to Shrine Mont and remained active in the church book club until the end of his life, not only recommending favorite books to friends far and wide but buying multiple copies and distributing them to those who had expressed interest. Bud’s involvement in prison ministry was a source of inspiration and quiet pride for him.

Active in many parts of his community, Bud served as the president of the Fairfax County Jaycees, the president of the Madison High School booster club, on the board of The Potomac School, on the Virginia State Bar Council and as a Big Brother. He was a longtime member of Westwood Country Club.

Bud was a delightful friend, charming all who met him, quickly putting strangers at ease and touching many lives with his genuine interest. As the saying goes, he never met a stranger and those who knew him are all the better for it. He could never say no to anyone who needed help. A devoted father, Bud was an inspired coach, an involved sideline cheerleader, and a patient and wise guide to life. He is known by his sons for his goofy and quirky sense of humor, sometimes deemed (wonderfully) inappropriate by his wife. Laughter was a staple of his marriage with Lisa; the joy and appreciation they had for each other is an inspiration.

We were privileged to call Bud our partner, and blessed to call him our friend. Although the community has lost one of its most cherished members, the lessons and skills that he taught us and lived by will carry on as a tribute to his remarkable life.

attorneys.name: Jeff W. Rosen
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Rosen is a firm shareholder who focuses on civil litigation, local government, labor and employment, and insurance defense.

An experienced trial lawyer and former prosecutor, Jeff successfully defends claims regarding civil rights violations, medical malpractice, wrongful death suits against Virginia sheriffs and regional jails, and excessive force claims against law enforcement. Jeff specializes in representing state and local governments and their employees in cases involving constitutional violations, employment discrimination, defamation, and tort claims against cities, towns, school boards and regional authorities.

He is a former Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney and a frequent lecturer for the Virginia Sheriff's Association and the Virginia Association of Regional Jails on issues relating to law enforcement, employment law and correctional medical issues. Jeff is also an instructor at the Hampton Roads Law Enforcement Training Academy

REPRESENTATIVE CASES & TRANSACTIONS

Jeff has defended over 350 cases alleging Civil Rights and Title VII employment discrimination claims, including claims of wrongful death, excessive force, police shooting and failure to provide adequate medical care to prisoners.

He has obtained favorable outcomes for Virginia sheriffs, regional jails, state and local governments and the insurance industry in both federal and state court. He has over 63 reported federal and state cases, and he has appeared before the Supreme Court of Virginia and United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit on numerous occasions.

attorneys.name: Charlotte R. Rosen
attorneys.practice_type: Government Contracts Law Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
For over three decades, Charlotte Rosen has been helping government contractors of all sizes and in many industries find business-oriented solutions to legal problems relating to their government contracts. She provides efficient service and quick turn-around, advice on all kinds of day-to-day procurement issues, and experienced representation in government audits, litigation, and investigations.

Charlotte's experience spans the entire life cycle of a government contract. She advises businesses regarding pre-solicitation notices and solicitation requirements and how to best use pre-award processes such as Q&As, NAICS assignments, and size certification matters to best posture the client in the competition. Before contract award, she ensures that all facets of an impending deal, such as teaming relationships and workshare/workforce concerns, and protection of client data rights and software, best reflect the client's interests. After award, she helps clients with compliance and reporting questions; creative solutions to subcontract enforcement and disputes; and to evaluate, prepare, and settle or litigate REAs, disputes and claims before the Boards of Contract Appeals and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims. She has litigated numerous defensive and offensive bid protests at the agency level and before the Government Accountability Office and the Court of Federal Claims, as well as size protests to Contracting Officers and the SBA. Additionally, she has expertise in federal grant programs.

Her clients include small and large professional and IT services providers, technology developers and research-focused firms, and businesses in the defense and transportation industries. She represents clients who are participants in SBA programs as well as non-profits, including AbilityOne organizations.

Prior to practicing government contracts law with major DC area law firms, Charlotte served as an Assistant General Counsel with the Navy Office of the General Counsel.

attorneys.name: Hope Rosen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Hope Rosen's practice has consistently centered on child and family law issues. After receiving her law degree, Ms. Rosen worked as a staff attorney for the American Prosecutors Research Institute, focusing on issues of juvenile delinquency and child abuse. Ms. Rosen left the American Prosecutors Research Institute when she was appointed Special Counsel for the Division of Child Support Enforcement by the Attorney General of Virginia. After building her expertise in child support law, Ms. Rosen expanded her family law practice to include matters of child custody and visitation, protective orders, spousal support and equitable distribution of marital assets and liabilities. In addition to Ms. Rosen's experience in litigation, she is also trained in collaborative law, which allows her to offer her skills in various approaches to dispute resolution.

Ms. Rosen received her Bachelor of Arts from the College of William and Mary and her Juris Doctor from the George Mason University School of Law. During her graduate work, she served as president of George Mason's trial advocacy team. Since she has been in practice, Ms. Rosen has been recognized by Super Lawyers as a rising star every year since 2009.

Ms. Rosen is a member of the Virginia State Bar, the Circuit Court Committee of the Fairfax Bar Association, Prince William County Bar Association, Virginia Women's Attorney Association, and the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association (VTLA). She has appeared in Juvenile and Domestic Relations District Courts and Circuit Courts throughout Northern Virginia, and she has appeared before the Virginia Court of Appeals in matters relating to child support, spousal support and equitable distribution. Ms. Rosen has been admitted to practice law in the Commonwealth of Virginia since 2002.

In her free time, Ms. Rosen volunteers her time as a conciliator for the Conciliation Program, which is a free service offered by the Fairfax Bar Association. She has also provided pro bono services for victims of domestic violence through the Civil Protection Order program offered by Legal Services of Northern Virginia.

attorneys.name: Faraji A. Rosenthall Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in McLean, VA
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Faraji Rosenthall has devoted his career to the criminal justice system in Northern Virginia. Following completion of his education, Mr. Rosenthall served as Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney in Fairfax County. In this role, he prosecuted countless criminal cases, ranging from traffic offenses to felony-level robbery and manslaughter. In 2009, Mr. Rosenthall followed in his father’s footsteps and made the transition to the defense side of the criminal justice system.

CAPTURING THE ESSENCE OF A CLIENT, ONE STORY AT A TIME

Born and raised in the Alexandria area, Faraji Rosenthall prides himself on his ability to relate to his clients. His goal is to set you at ease during what must be a frightening and confusing point in your life.

To do this, Mr. Rosenthall sets aside ego and judgment. Then he sits back and listens—truly listens—to your story. He wants to know where you’re at and where you’ve come from, what you’re feeling and what you’re worried about, and where you hope your future will take you.

By capturing your true essence, Faraji can tell your story effectively to the courts. And it is your story that will be the difference. It is your story that will be the linchpin that sways a judge or jury to offer mercy and leniency.

NO FALSE PROMISES, ONLY HARD WORK

There are no guarantees of an outcome when it comes to your legal problems. (If only that were not true!) But there is a way to put your best foot forward. Through dedicated representation and continual contact, you can rest assured knowing Mr. Rosenthall is asserting his best efforts to support you. You will have an advocate who will fight hard for you against a complicated and often unforgiving system.

attorneys.name: Linda K. Rosenthal
attorneys.practice_type: Securities Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Linda Rosenthal has extensive experience with private offerings, including private placements and small offerings, as well as public offerings. She counsels clients on complying with the federal and state securities laws, including those relating to the issuance, purchase and sale of restricted and control securities. She organizes internal securities markets involving companies, their employees and shareholders, and assists clients in establishing compensatory benefit plans relating to the issuance of options, warrants, appreciation rights, restricted stock and units, and other restricted securities. Linda also prepares Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and state securities filings and assists clients under investigation by the SEC and the Virginia Division of Securities and Retail Franchising. In addition, she counsels clients regarding compliance with federal and state laws applicable to investment advisers, solicitors, finders, and securities brokers.

Linda also has experience with a broad range of transactional and general corporate matters. She counsels clients regarding mergers, stock, and asset acquisitions, as well as for a wide variety of purchase, sales, lending, investment and joint venture transactions. She also provides advice regarding complex financial arrangements and non-bankruptcy restructurings and reorganizations. In addition, she counsels for-profit and tax-exempt clients about a wide variety of matters relating to the organization and operation of their businesses, including advice on business structure and formation, corporate governance, and compliance with state business acts and commercial codes.

Nathan D. Rozsa is a native of Fairfax County, Virginia. He is licensed to practice before all Virginia courts. Mr. Rozsa graduated from the University of Virginia School of Law in 2008, and was licensed to practice in the Commonwealth of Virginia the same year. attorneys.name: Ella Russell
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Leesburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Legal Practice

Ella Russell is an attorney at Sevila, Saunders, Huddleston, & White P.C., specializing in family and immigration law. In her family law practice, she prioritizes her clients’ goals, conducting a thorough cost-benefit analysis to inform client decisions and employing a tailored approach to each case. Ms. Russell handles a variety of family matters, including divorce, custody and visitation, support, equitable distribution, protective orders, marital agreements, retirement/pension division, same-sex marriage and divorce, international divorce and custody issues, and adoption.

In immigration law, Ms. Russell draws from her personal experience as a first-generation immigrant to provide compassionate and effective representation. She advocates for clients in family-based petitions, Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS) cases, asylum applications, and citizenship matters. Licensed in Virginia and Maryland, she is fluent in Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian, with conversational proficiency in Spanish.

Community Leadership

Ms. Russell is dedicated to community service, serving as President of the Loudoun Chapter of the Virginia Women Attorneys Association (VWAA) and as a former Board Member of the Washington Council of Lawyers (WCL) (2022-2023). She was recognized as a Virginia Rising Star for 2024 by Super Lawyers for her contributions to the legal field.

Pro Bono and Law School Experience

During law school, Ms. Russell was actively involved in pro bono work, including serving as an Equal Justice Works Fellow with Legal Services of Greater Miami, interning with the Public Defender's Office, participating in the Immigration Litigation Clinic, and volunteering with Just Neighbors.

Virginia Super Lawyers, Rising Star; 2024 - 2025

attorneys.bio:
Daniel H. Ruttenberg is a principal with the firm. He is a member of the Bar in Virginia, Maryland and the District of Columbia, and is licensed as a Certified Public Accountant in by the State of Maryland. Mr. Ruttenberg received his Bachelor of Science degree with a double major in Accounting and Finance from the University of Maryland. He earned his Juris Doctor with Honors from George Mason University School of Law and his Master of Laws in Taxation with Distinction from Georgetown University Law Center.

Mr. Ruttenberg is the author of "The Tax Court's Execution of the Family Entity: The Tax Court's Application of Internal Revenue Code Section 2036(a) to Family Entities," North Dakota Law Review Vol. 80:41 (2004). For the past six years, he has served as Vice President of Devotion To Children, a charity which provides access to high-quality educational and childcare programs for children from low-income families, aged six and under. Mr. Ruttenberg served as the Director of the Fairfax Bar Association (FBA) for seven years. During this period, he was also elected president - the youngest in FBA history. He also served as a member of the Board of Directors for the Fairfax Law Foundation. Mr. Ruttenberg received a SmartCEO Magazine Power Player award in 2013 and 2014, and was named a Top Lawyer by Northern Virginia Magazine in 2015, 2013, 2010 and 2009. Most recently, he was selected as one of the 2015 and 2016 "Best Lawyers in America" by Best Lawyers.

His practice areas include: planning for businesses, general corporate law, estate planning and estate administration.

His background includes 15 years (1992 to 2007) of litigating on behalf of clients in cases throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia while working at Kalfus & Nachman. He then served for more than 7 years as the Head of the Litigation Section in the Hampton City Attorney’s office as a Deputy and then Senior Deputy City Attorney in that office. While in this role, he was honored to have been chosen by the Hampton City Council to serve, for a brief period, as the Acting City Attorney for the City of Hampton. Attorney Sachs also worked for several years as a staff counsel for a large national insurance company and as an independent, privately contracted insurance defense counsel. Ultimately, he was drawn back to the passion for protecting the wrongfully injured shared by our team at Kalfus & Nachman.

Mr. Sachs’ experience from both sides of the courtroom and both sides of the legal process provides him with unique insights into what his clients can expect as any case develops. Kalfus & Nachman does everything possible to help our clients recover the maximum amount for their cases, which is a goal shared by Attorney Sachs. He prides himself on his willingness to take the time to truly listen to his clients, enabling them to feel confident as their case proceeds.

For his outstanding work and representation, Attorney Jeffry Sachs has been honored to be named to Virginia Business Magazine's Legal Elite list.

Mr. Sachs completed his undergraduate studies in Criminal Justice at Old Dominion University in Norfolk, Virginia. He went on to earn his law degree at the Delaware Law School of Widener University in Wilmington, Delaware.

In his spare time, Jeffry enjoys spending his time with his wife, Lynn, and visiting their incredibly gifted and talented daughters Sara and Rachel, whenever they can.

attorneys.name: Lily Saffer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Falls Church, VA
attorneys.bio:
Lily Saffer joined the Firm as an associate attorney in August 2020. Prior to joining Maddox & Gerock, Lily worked for nearly five years as an associate with Surovell Isaacs & Levy PLC, building extensive experience as a family law attorney, as well as representing numerous clients in civil matters such as contract disputes, landlord tenant cases, and consumer protection suits. This additional experience has broadened Lily's familiarity with all areas of the law, many of which impact family law cases.

Lily grew up in Seattle, Washington and graduated from Wellesley College in Massachusetts cum laude in 2010. Lily then went on to the William & Mary Marshall-Wythe School of Law as a Graduate Research Fellow. Throughout her time at William & Mary, Lily worked extensively with the Children's Advocacy Law Society, served as a research assistant to family law professor James Dwyer, and spent both her summers interning with Legal Aid organizations. After graduating from William & Mary in 2013, Lily served for two years as the law clerk to the Hon. Dennis J. Smith, who was then Chief Judge of the Fairfax County Circuit Court, then to the Hon. Penney S. Azcarate in the same Court after Chief Judge Smith's retirement. Lily entered the active practice of law in September 2015.

Throughout her career, Lily has litigated cases in Juvenile & Domestic Relations District Courts; General District Courts; Circuit Courts; and the Virginia Court of Appeals. In 2022 Lily received the Pro Bono Champion Award from the Fairfax Bar Association; in 2023 Lily received the Service Above Self award from the Rotary Club of Fairfax. Lily has been selected as a Virginia Lawyers Rising Star in Family Law by Super Lawyers every year since 2019.

Lily has extensive experience in all areas of family law, including divorce, equitable distribution, child custody and visitation, child support establishment and modification, spousal support establishment and modification, and drafting of prenuptial, postnuptial, and separation agreements.

Lily can also assist with estate planning, an important step for anyone entering into or ending a marriage or welcoming a new child to the family. Lily provides simple estate planning services for Virginia residents, including Last Will and Testament, Advance Medical Directive, Durable Power of Attorney, and simple Trusts.

Lily lives in Ann Arbor, Michigan (practicing Virginia law remotely) with her husband, two children, and dog named Butters.

attorneys.name: Aram A. Sahakyan
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Aram Sahakyan is an associate in OFP’s commercial real estate practice.

Aram earned his J.D. from George Mason University’s Antonin Scalia Law School, where he was a Mason Scholarship recipient. He holds a B.A. in Philosophy, with minors in Legal Studies and Global Studies, from Colorado State University, where he graduated with Dean’s List honors across eight semesters.

Aram brings significant experience in real estate and housing matters. As a legal intern with the Montgomery County Department of Housing and Community Affairs, he researched land records, negotiated loan restructures, drafted legal correspondence, and worked with county attorneys on secured property interests. He has also worked in real estate development as an executive assistant with Structure Realty LLC and operated his own service business supporting members of his local community.

Earlier in his career, Aram coordinated facilities operations for Sidwell Friends School in Washington, D.C., and served as a Senior Associate Facilitator for Colorado State’s Center for Public Deliberation, where he led community dialogue events and trained new facilitators. He is fluent in Armenian.

attorneys.name: Michael Salasky
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Norfolk, VA
attorneys.bio:
Michael Salasky has proudly represented families in Virginia and provided advocacy since 1977.

Born and raised in Norfolk, Virginia, Michael attended Norfolk Academy and graduated college from Tufts University in Boston where he received a B.A. in English. He received his law degree from the Marshall-Wythe School of Law at the College of William and Mary in 1977. For several years he worked as an Assistant Commonwealth’s Attorney in Norfolk and prosecuted all varieties of criminal cases, from traffic matters to murder cases.

After a two year stint as an associate in a private law office, he opened his own law practice in 1982. Before concentrating his work in cases involving injuries, Michael gained a wealth of experience over the years handling divorce and custody matters, real estate, collections, bankruptcy, construction law, contract matters, criminal cases and other disputes.

Over the years he has participated in the American Association For Justice, the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, the American Bar Association, and local civic organizations.

He is married to Prue Salasky, who is a journalist and editorial writer. They have three daughters.

attorneys.name: Monica Sameni
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Sameni joined the firm in 2023 as an associate practicing family law. During law school, she served as a certified student attorney at her school’s legal clinic, with a focus on domestic law and tax law matters. Following law school, Ms. Sameni served as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Michael F. Devine at the Circuit Court of Fairfax County. In this role, Ms. Sameni developed a deep understanding of the intricacies of the legal system.

As an active participant in the legal community, Ms. Sameni was recently elected to serve in the board of directors for the Fairfax Bar Association Young Lawyers Section. Ms. Sameni’s service underscores her commitment to promoting excellence and camaraderie among young lawyers in Fairfax County.

Ms. Sameni was raised in Fairfax, Virginia, completed her undergraduate studies at West Virginia University, and graduated from the Catholic University Columbus School of Law. She resides in Fairfax County with her husband. Ms. Sameni is a member of the bar of Virginia and the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.
