attorneys.name: Craig W. Sampson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
Craig W. Sampson is a President & Shareholder at Barnes & Diehl, P.C. in Richmond, Virginia. He is a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers (Chicago). He handles complex divorce, custody, and support matters in courts throughout the Commonwealth. Before joining Barnes & Diehl, he was the principal of Sampson Law Firm, P.L.C., where he handled family law matters and criminal cases at all levels of the state and federal systems, including successful petitions for writ of certiorari to the United States Supreme Court. He is a past president of the Metro Richmond Family Law Bar Association. He lectures semi-annually on the Updates in the Law at the Advanced Family Law Seminar hosted by Virginia CLE, and he has presented on multiple occasions at the Bench Bar Conference in Richmond. Craig has published many articles over the years in the Virginia Family Law Quarterly. He was an adjunct professor of Family Law Ethics at the University of Richmond School of Law from 2017 to 2019, and he was a recipient of the 2017 Leader in the Law Award. He currently serves on the Board of Governors for the Family Law Section of the Virginia State Bar. He is also a co-author of the family law treatise known as "Virginia Practice: Family Law -Theory Practice and Forms" which is published annually by Thomson Reuters.

attorneys.name: Robert L. Samuel
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Defense Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Bob Samuel is a firm shareholder who oversees all workers' compensation cases. He focuses his practice in the areas of personal injury and litigation.

Bob has handled more than 125 jury trials since he began representing clients in 1979, and has earned an outstanding reputation from his clients and peers. He routinely advises municipalities and businesses assessing the merits of workers' compensation and injury cases and the risks of defense. His practice focuses on complex personal injury matters on behalf of defendents and representation of inidivudals injured as a result of the negligence of others. Bob regularly appears before the Virginia Workers' Compensation Commission and Circuit Courts in the Commonwealth of Virginia.

Frequently asked to lead continuing legal education seminars and speak on the topics of workers' compensation and personal injury law, Bob also serves as a consultant for municipalities and third party administrators in workers' compensation cases.

REPRESENTATIVE CASES & TRANSACTIONS

Represented municipality in $20 million litigation where the plaintiff suffered catastrophic injuries, alleged negligence and punitive damages arising out of a motor vehicle accident with a police officer.

Represented deputy sheriff in $625,000 personal injury case after he suffered severe injuries in a motor vehicle accident when responding to an emergency call with lights and sirens.

Represented development company and its president in $5 million litigation with former employer alleging breach of fiduciary duty in the purchase and development of land project.

Represented municipality in an occupational disease workers' compensation claim where the claimant alleged the need for a heart transplant arose from heart disease caused by his employment with the municipality.

Represented local transit company in million-dollar litigation brought by a passenger alleging post-traumatic stress disorder and permanent back impairment to his back due to injury on the transit bus.

attorneys.name: P. Todd Sartwell
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
With over 20 years in the legal field, P. Todd Sartwell is a seasoned trial attorney known for diligent representation, strategic thinking, and skilled negotiations. A partner at Dickerson and Smith Law Group, he brings decades of experience at both the state and federal levels. Mr. Sartwell’s legal skills and professional reputation have been recognized multiple times by the prestigious Super Lawyer magazine.

Mr. Sartwell’s breadth of knowledge allows him to effectively represent clients with a wide spectrum of legal challenges and he has a varied portfolio of cases; however, his core practice is based in personal injury, family law, criminal defense, employment law (including workers’ compensation), and estate planning. He also provides support for clients during their SSDI Appeal hearings.

Clients value Mr. Sartwell for his practical advice and ability to bring clarity to the legal process. He often takes the lead in negotiations in order to obtain the best outcome for his clients; however, with his extensive trial experience, he does not shy away from courtroom battles when negotiations stall and litigation is the best path forward. Whether defending the accused, fighting for fair compensation after an injury, or navigating complex divorce or custody issues, Mr. Sartwell provides compassionate, tenacious, and results-driven representation.

attorneys.name: Thomas J. Sawyer
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Law Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Throughout his more than 30-year career, Tom has represented employers in a broad spectrum of employment matters, including wage and hour, discrimination, and employee termination. He is known particularly for his employee defection work, including drafting and enforcing non-competes and other employment-based restrictive covenants, and litigating related contract, fiduciary duty, trade secret, tortious interference, conspiracy, and unfair competition disputes.

Tom's clients include national and international companies, as well as numerous local companies based in the Washington, D.C. area. He has particularly deep experience counseling technology and government contracting companies on employment issues and representing them in related litigation.

Prior to joining the firm, Tom was the head of the Labor & Employment practice of a 1,300-attorney, international law firm and the co-founding partner of its Northern Virginia office.

Tom has long been recognized as a leading employment lawyer, including by Chambers, Best Lawyers in America, International Who's Who of Management Labour & Employment Lawyers, and Martindale-Hubbell. He has also spoken often on employee defection and other employment topics to law and industry groups, including the American Bar Association, Association for Corporate Counsel, and the Washington Metropolitan Area Corporate Counsel Association.

attorneys.name: Benjamin Schaefer
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ben Schaefer is a skilled defense attorney who specializes in financial crimes. After focusing his studies on business law in school, Mr. Schaefer began his career working with the Securities and Exchange Commission in Washington, D.C.. Since entering private practice, he has increasingly focused on white collar offenses such as fraud, false pretenses, grand larceny, forgery, identity theft, and embezzlement. He has had several recent high-profile legal victories, including an appeal to Virginia's Court of Appeals, which he won on a previously uncited legal argument.

Prosecutors in Northern Virginia are very serious about theft and financial crimes and have expert attorneys who specialize in prosecuting those offenses. The good news is that financial crimes are extremely complicated, and can be difficult to prosecute against a defense attorney who understands the many defenses that may apply. Bottom line: if you are charged with a financial crime, you need a defense attorney who also specializes in this sort of case.

attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Coverage and Defense Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Dan Schieble focuses his practice in the areas of litigation and personal injury.

Dan has more than 33 years' experience as a civil litigation attorney, handling over 100 jury trials to verdict. His litigation practice areas focus on plaintiff and defense personal injury and insurance coverage and defense. Dan represents clients in all State and Federal Courts of the Commonwealth. In addition to trial work, Dan advocates for clients on a regular basis utilizing mediation and arbitration.

Dan was elected to the Virginia State Bar Council in 2013 and is currently in his second term. He represents the interests of attorneys and the public for Virginia's Second Judicial District regarding regulation of the legal profession and public access to legal services. Dan is a past member and chairman of the Second District Disciplinary Committee and past member of the Virginia Beach Bar Association Medical-Legal Liaison Committee.

attorneys.name: Erin N. Schiffman
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Litigation Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Erin N. Schiffman is an Associate at Odin Feldman Pittleman, where she focuses her practice on employment law and trade secret litigation, handling both transactional and courtroom matters. Erin believes that the law should be a tool for clarity, fairness, and problem-solving—not confusion. With these things in mind, she advises employers on personnel policies, negotiates severance and employment agreements, conducts workplace investigations, and represents clients in employment litigation, restrictive covenant disputes, and trade secret misappropriation cases.

Erin’s practice blends a sharp eye for detail with a practical, business-minded approach to help clients see the big picture, understand their options, and move forward with confidence—whether that means resolving matters quietly, negotiating favorable settlements, or litigating when necessary. She has gained substantial experience representing businesses and individuals in high-stakes litigation, including successfully resolving multimillion-dollar trade secret and employment disputes before state and federal courts. Her transactional work includes crafting and negotiating agreements that protect clients’ interests while ensuring compliance with employment laws.

A native of the DC-metro area, Erin comes from a family of attorneys, including her parents and brother. Erin graduated cum laude from the University of Maryland, Francis King Carey School of Law, where she concentrated her studies on business, employment, and disability/special education law. Her passion for disability and employment law led her to the Civil Rights of Persons with Disabilities Clinic, where she provided legal assistance and advice to clients with disabilities in conjunction with the National Association of the Deaf and supervised other clinic students.

Prior to joining the firm, Erin was an associate at a boutique business and employment law firm in Fairfax, Virginia.

Outside of her regular practice, Erin is passionate about helping students obtain accommodations in school and testing-related settings ranging from pre-K through professional licensing exams. She is also a board member of The Arc of Northern Virginia and co-chairs the Employment Law Forum for the Women’s Bar Association of the District of Columbia.

In her free time, Erin enjoys horseback riding, spending time with her family and three-pound Yorkie, doing art, and baking.

attorneys.name: Sean P. Schmergel
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Arlington, VA
attorneys.bio:
Sean P. Schmergel has been consistently recognized as one the DMVs top divorce and family law attorneys, including by Washingtonian Magazine, Arlington Magazine, Super Lawyers and U.S. News's Best Lawyers. He co-founded Schmergel & Mersberger, PLC over 20 years ago and has continued to hone his legal practice before the local courts, developing a reputation as a zealous and thoughtful family law advocate. A resident of Northern Virginia for over 30 years, Mr. Schmergel holds a genuine concern for the legal matters that affect the members of his community, and he devotes his practice to helping families throughout the Northern Virginia jurisdictions of Arlington, Alexandria, Fairfax, Prince William and Loudoun, as well as Washington, D.C., with all of their complex and emotional legal challenges.

Focusing exclusively on family law, Mr. Schmergel has achieved extraordinary success advocating on behalf of the rights and best interests of those he serves who are going through divorce or other family law cases, helping them with their issues involving child custody and support, alimony, property division, and other related matters. He also delivers effective prenuptial and other marital agreements, assists with modifications and enforcements, and provides much-needed support for domestic abuse victims seeking protections for themselves and their children, or those wrongly accused and in need of a vigorous defense.

Mr. Schmergel has extensive experience settling cases through mediation and other forms of alternative dispute resolution, helping his clients resolve their conflicts and reach agreements without the need for costly, drawn-out litigation; however, as a highly-rated and seasoned trial attorney, he will not hesitate to fight hard on behalf of his clients in court when necessary. He has litigated many high-conflict divorce and child custody cases, including international custody disputes. As a father, Mr. Schmergel holds a particular concern for children caught in the divorce process as well as for those in abusive situations, and he serves as guardian ad litem for children throughout Northern Virginia.

A 1996 graduate of George Mason University with a Bachelor of Arts in government and politics, Mr. Schmergel returned to his alma mater and attended George Mason University School of Law. After obtaining his Juris Doctor in 2000 he was admitted to practice in Virginia and subsequently admitted in Washington, D.C., as well as to the bars of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia and the United States Supreme Court.

Active in his legal community, he is the past president of the Alexandria Bar Association and serves on Alexandria’s Judicial Screening Committee. He currently serves on the Virginia State Bar’s District 4-II Disciplinary Committee and was the Chair from 2016-2018. He is a member of the Arlington County Bar Association and the Family Law Sections of the Virginia State Bar and The District of Columbia Bar.

attorneys.name: Catherine F. Schott Murray
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Reston, VA
attorneys.bio:
Begin the Begin - Once you begin you are closer to the end than had you not begun at all. With that statement, Catherine F. Schott Murray appreciates that every client's situation is unique and requires solutions that are adapted to their particular needs, goals, and objectives once the planning process has begun. She takes the time to carefully listen to her clients and discuss decisions that are not always straightforward, ultimately reaching an appropriate resolution that is pertinent to each client. Catherine is professional, yet compassionate, while carefully explaining complex matters during potentially trying times.

Catherine's practice focuses on trust and estate planning as well as business planning. She advises clients with respect to the creation and implementation of simple and complex estate plans, including incapacity planning; elder law; guardianships and conservatorships; special needs trusts; health care decision making; estate and trust administration; probate administration; wealth preservation; asset protection; entity formation and maintenance, gift, estate and generation-skipping transfer tax planning; charitable planning; irrevocable trusts; donor advised funds; private foundations; family limited partnerships; and limited liability companies.

Prior to joining the firm, Catherine assisted individuals with estate planning and Medicaid planning as well as represented lenders and closely held companies in commercial and financial transactions, commercial lease negotiations, mergers and acquisitions, bankruptcy, commercial litigation, and collections.

Catherine has been an active member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA) and served on the Board of Directors of the Virginia Chapter (VAELA) of NAELA for more than a decade, including time spent as the organization's President.

Catherine gives back to the community through her involvement with the Community Foundation for Northern Virginia (CFNOVA) in which she has served on the Board of Directors, including as the Board Chair.

Outside of the office, Catherine volunteers her time with her children's school and enjoys roads trips with her family.

attorneys.name: Theseus Schulze
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Theseus Schulze, an esteemed attorney, is renowned for his adeptness in simplifying intricate legal matters into easily comprehensible terms. Committed to ensuring that every client gains a comprehensive understanding of potential outcomes, Theseus takes pride in delivering honest and concise advice. Clients often commend him for providing the perspective they may not have wanted to hear but genuinely needed.

Known for his casual style, Theseus frequently arrives at the office early, clad in classic jeans and Timberland boots. A native of Northern Virginia, he graduated from Loudoun County High School, back when their mascot was the Raiders. Beyond his legal pursuits, Theseus has an impressive background in strongman competitions, powerlifting, muay thai, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and MMA. He continues to maintain his fighting shape by lifting stones and flipping tires in his Loudoun County garage while training at American Top Team. When not working or training, he enjoys spending time with his wife and three Australian shepherds.

In his legal practice, Theseus specializes in various aspects of family law, including custody, divorce, separation, prenuptial agreements, and adoption. Additionally, his expertise extends to criminal law, traffic cases, protective orders, as well as estate planning.

attorneys.bio:
GERALD SCHWARTZ – SPECIALIZING IN PERSONAL INJURY & WRONGFUL DEATH LAW

Gerald Schwartz specializes in representing people seriously injured and families who have lost a love one because of someone else’s negligence. That’s all Mr. Schwartz does. Nothing else. For over 30 years, Mr. Schwartz has helped people with life changing injuries from auto, truck and motorcycle accidents fight for justice. Gerald Schwartz is an aggressive, compassionate, and caring advocate for his clients.

Gerald Schwartz has extensive experience in handling brain injury, nerve injury, herniated disc, fracture, and serious orthopedic and neurologic injury cases requiring surgery.

Gerald Schwartz has a state-wide reputation of being a leader in personal injury and wrongful death law. He is often asked to teach other personal injury and wrongful death lawyers how to maximize recovery in serious injury and wrongful death cases. Personal injury lawyers throughout the state often call Mr. Schwartz for advice on how to handle their cases. Gerald Schwartz is a past President of the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association. In 2019, he received the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association’ prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award.

Call Gerald Schwartz for a free consultation for straight answers to your legal questions.

attorneys.name: Douglas Scott
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy - Chapter 11 Reorganization Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
My family moved frequently as I was growing up because of my father's Navy orders. Among other places, we were stationed in Florida, California, Texas, and Virginia. It took me 11 years to graduate from high school (Some would say that had nothing to do with the moving). After my dad retired, we moved to Oxford, Mississippi during the peak of the civil rights storm, Later, we moved to rural North Carolina, where I developed my fondness for pork barbecue, aimless road trips, and that special, curious accent that North Carolinians develop.

I attended college, graduate school and law school in North Carolina; it was there that I spent the first eight years of my law practice. It was challenging work, representing, I moved to Richmond, Virginia to manage one, and then another, civil legal aid program.

In due course, I had one of my periodic mid-life crises, and left legal aid to work as a business lawyer for a mid-Sized downtown Richmond law firm. I worked my way from associate to partner during these years, and the focus of my practice turned to business bankruptcy and bankruptcy litigation. I like the practice because I seldom do the same thing twice

My oldest daughter, Elizabeth, graduated several years ago with distinction from St.John's college in Annapolis, One of the last of the great books curriculum schools in the country. Elizabeth now lives in Chicago, where she is a graduate comic book artist who will do well in her art career so long as it does not involve math of any flavor

I continue apace. I am still behind on the Fourth Five Year Plan to renovate my house in North Side Richmond. I have culled out my collection of old BMW and Volvo automobiles because the garage will not hold any more parts. There is hope yet.

I started my own Commercial bankruptcy practice a several years ago, and I'm quite happy with it, it's just me, so I always know where the blame should lie. About three years ago, I spent six months flat on my back due to a head injury. Like the old joke, I still can't play the piano. Things are now back to a familiar, but nevertheless warped, normality. Thank goodness.

I am still on the right side of the grass, as it was expressed to me recently, but somewhere along the line I lost my sense of smell. Good exchange, it seems to me.

I am still on the right side of the grass, as it was expressed to me recently, but somewhere along the line I lost my sense of smell. Good exchange, it seems to me.

attorneys.name: Jamie B. Sexton
attorneys.practice_type: Business valuation Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
At first meeting it will become apparent that Jamie Sexton is a compassionate, straight forward lawyer who has your best interest in mind. With over 20 years experience representing clients in family law matters in Richmond and the surrounding areas, she is tenacious problem solver and you will feel confident knowing she is on your side.

Jamie completed her undergraduate education at North Carolina State University earning a B.A. in History, Magna Cum Laude, and then went on to graduate from the University of Richmond School of Law in 2002. After graduating law school she worked alongside some of the most respected family law attorneys in the area until eventually founding her own firm in 2007. For several years Jamie also served as a Guardian ad litem for children in custody cases, which meant that she worked closely with children, the parties, all counsel on the cases, therapists, custody evaluators, co-parenting coaches and many others that often are involved in custody matters. This gave her insight into all facets of those matters and experience that is invaluable in those cases.

Jamie has been an active member of the Bar Association of the City of Richmond since graduating law school and has served on and chaired numerous committees including the Bench Bar Planning committee, Continuing Legal Education committee and Publications committee. She is also actively involved in the Metro Women's Bar Association, Metro Richmond Family Law Bar Association and Virginia Trial Lawyers Association. She continues active involvement with the University of Richmond School of Law serving on the Young Graduates Board, participating in mock interview programs for students, serving as judge for competitions and mentoring law students. Jamie has also given her time for probono legal work through the Legal Aid Justice Center Housing Law unit.

Jamie has been selected as a "Rising Star" by Super Lawyers and was also selected by Virginia Business as one of Virginia's "Legal Elite". Outside of the practice of law she spends time with family and friends and is also an avid runner.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey A. Shane MD, J.D
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Dr. Jeffrey A. Shane is a distinguished physician and attorney specializing in obstetrics and gynecology. He also has extensive experience in medical malpractice law. Dr. Shane received his MD from the Boston University School of Medicine in 1968, and performed his residency subsequently form 1969 to 1973. He completed his residency at the Bronx Municipal Hospital Center and has been board certified in both obstetrics and gynecology, as well as medical law. Dr Shane has worked with Weiner, Spivey and Miller PLC for several years as a medical-legal consultant.

Dr. Shane is also a former service member. He is a retired Colonel from the United States Air Force, serving various military and academic positions, these included faculty roles at multiple universities. He has published extensively on topics ranging from the medical-legal ramifications of difficult labor and delivery to guidelines for obstetricians facing malpractice crises. His notable works include “The Female Reproductive System – An Overview” in the Lawyers’ Medical Journal and “How Prenatal Genetic Testing Protects Patients – And You” in OBG management.

He has delivered over 100 presentations focusing on patient safety, quality assurance, and several other topics in the medical-legal field. His presentations included “Mitigating Legal Risks in Obstetric Practice”, and “Quality Assurance in Obstetrics: Best Practices”. He is currently working as a consultant specializing in patient safety and risk management, while contributing as a Fellow for the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, as well as the American College of Legal Medicine. He has had significant impact in the field of law and medicine throughout his career and has continued to play an active role in the medical-legal community.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Ellen Sharpe believes most commercial real estate transactions should be win-win. Her approach involves common-sense solutions and the ability to see down the road for her clients. Ellen's practice encompasses all areas of commercial real estate transactions, including representing buyers and sellers in the acquisition, sale, and financing of raw and improved commercial property. She represents both landlords and tenants in office, industrial, retail, and ground leasing, and represents both lenders and borrowers in real estate finance transactions. She has worked with property owners and investors, trade and nonprofit associations, homebuilders, office, industrial and retail developers, data centers, lenders, and all types of businesses in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan area regarding the disposition and financing of commercial property. Ellen's practice also focuses on development law, including the creation of condominiums, mixed-use projects, shopping centers, and planned unit developments. She has also acted as an arbitrator in commercial lease disputes.

She lives in Arlington, Virginia, with her husband and two sons.

attorneys.name: J. Thompson Shrader
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Amherst, VA
attorneys.bio:
J. THOMPSON SHRADER, is a native of Amherst County, graduating from Amherst County High School in 1971. He received his B.A. in 1975 from the University of Richmond and his J.D. in 1979 from the T.C. Williams School of Law at the University of Richmond. He also attended the University of Richmond Graduate School of Business.

In addition to his regular legal practice, Mr. Shrader serves as Commissioner of Accounts for Amherst and Nelson Counties and is a former Escheator for Amherst County, giving him a unique perspective on real estate and estate planning issues facing his clients. He is also a Commissioner in Chancery for both counties. Mr. Shrader has also served as County Attorney for the County of Amherst and currently serves as attorney for the Amherst County Department of Social Services.

Before starting his law practice, Mr. Shrader worked in the legal department of First Colony Life Insurance in Lynchburg (now Genworth), where he gained significant business law experience.

Mr. Shrader is a member of the Amherst-Nelson Bar Association, serving as treasurer since 1988, the Lynchburg Bar Association, and the Virginia State Bar Association.

Mr. Shrader supports non-profits in the Amherst community, providing pro bono services to a number of local organizations. He was an active firefighter with the Amherst Fire Department for 45 years, and has served as Chief.

attorneys.name: Thomas B. Shuttleworth
attorneys.firm_name: Ruloff, Swain, Haddad, Morecock, Talbert & Woodward, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty and Maritime Law Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Tom Shuttleworth is the senior partner in the firm. As the son of working class parents, he worked his way through college and law school in a variety of jobs including parking cars, waiting tables, working in construction, working in hospitals, as a police officer, and the law library.

Mr. Shuttleworth is a trial lawyer who tries both personal injury and criminal cases. He is admitted to the United States Supreme Court. He is a member of the Fourth Circuit Judicial Conference and has in the past served in leadership roles in the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association. He graduated in 1973 from Washington & Lee University Law School where he was a member of the Washington & Lee Law Review. He is listed in the Best Lawyers in America under both civil and criminal and is AV rated in The Martindale-Hubbell. He is one of the lawyers in Virginia Beach listed in the Legal Elite who has been listed under both civil and criminal law. He was chosen as the 2009 Personal Injury Lawyer of the year by Best Lawyers in America for the Norfolk/Virginia Beach area and he was chosen as the 2012 Medical Malpractice Plaintiff’s Lawyer of the year by Best Lawyers in America for the Norfolk/Virginia Beach area. He taught law for three years at William & Mary Law School .

Mr. Shuttleworth has tried several cases to million dollar verdicts, the latest being medical malpractice cases one for $2,000,000.00 for an anesthesia accident and one for $3,500,000.00 verdict for a child suffering from erbs palsy; he obtained a verdict of $5,000,000.00 for the wrongful death of a doctor; $2,100,000.00 for the loss of an eye; $1,000,000.00 for misdiagnosis of Lupus; $2,100,000.00 for the wrongful death of a mother in a medical malpractice case; $1,500,000.00 for a seaman who had both ankles broken in a fall; and was one of the lawyers who represented homeowners in a $33,000,000.00 settlement for "jet noise" from a nearby Navy base.

He has tried several cases to highly successful conclusions in maritime, medical malpractice, and personal injury cases as well as major felony criminal trials.

He has won acquittals in several major felony cases. He was successful in overturning the wrongful conviction of NBA basketball star Allen Iverson and having the case dismissed and expunged from Mr. Iverson's record. He and Bob Morecock, another member of the firm, tried the first criminal trial televised in Virginia and secured a manslaughter conviction in high profile first degree murder prosecution. He has secured acquittals or dismissals in seven first degree murder prosecutions. He has represented successfully defendants in the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals in cases reversed for Batson violations. He has appeared 20 times in either the Supreme Court of Virginia or the Fourth Circuit to argue cases on appeal. He currently has a case in which the U.S. Supreme Court has granted certiorari in a 6th Amendment case.

Best Lawyers, the oldest and most respected peer-review publication in the legal profession, named Tom Shuttleworth as the Norfolk Area Best Lawyers Personal Injury Litigator of the Year for 2009.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Petersburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
J.J. is a personal injury attorney with Allen & Allen currently representing clients in the Chesterfield and the Greater Richmond areas. With a diverse background in insurance defense and commercial litigation, J.J. has tried over 100 cases and has experience in courts throughout the Commonwealth of Virginia, as well as the Federal Court system. His practice is now devoted to protecting the interests of seriously injured individuals and their families in all varieties of personal injury cases including automobile accidents.

Prior to joining Allen & Allen, J.J. spent years representing defendants and insurance companies, giving him valuable insight into how insurance companies value and handle personal injury claims.

J.J. is a proud Duke Dog who received his B.B.A. in Economics with a concentration in Finance from James Madison University in Harrisonburg, Virginia. He received his Juris Doctor from the University of Richmond T.C. Williams School of Law, where he was a member of the Moot Court and Trial Advocacy Boards, as well as a semi-finalist in the 2013 Costello National Trial Competition.

J.J. grew up in a military family and lived in various states throughout the country as a child. He, however, spent the majority of his time growing up in Stafford and Fredericksburg, Virginia. J.J. is an Eagle Scout who enjoys getting outdoors, as well as playing and watching sports such as lacrosse, basketball, and golf. J.J. played guitar and keyboard in various garage bands growing up, and still likes to pick up the guitar from time to time.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Manassas, VA
attorneys.bio:
Ben is a partner in the Firm, has over twenty-one years of courtroom litigation experience, and he represents individuals in a wide variety of civil litigation matters; including, Divorce and other Family Law Matters such as Equitable Distribution, Child Custody and Visitation Matters, and Spousal Support and Child Support Matters; Personal Injury Claims, including Wrongful Death, Motor Vehicle Accidents, Premises Liability, Dog Bites, intentional Torts, Assaults, Slip and Fall Accidents and Medical Malpractice Claims; Real Estate Litigation, including claims arising from the breach of Real Estate Contracts, and Landlord-Tenant matters; Legal Malpractice Claims; Commercial Litigation, and other Civil Litigation matters.

Ben is a very knowledgeable and aggressive advocate who is well known by the attorneys and judges throughout Northern Virginia for his zealous representation and as one who is always prepared and strives to achieve the best possible outcome for his clients, whether through negotiation and settlement or through the trial to verdict and judgment.

Ben began his legal career in 1991, and for the first six years of his legal career defended individuals on behalf of a variety of insurance companies in the defense of personal injury claims. Since that time, Ben has utilized the knowledge he obtained working for the insurance companies to the advantage of families who have tragically lost a loved one in a car accident or on behalf of those injured through the negligence of others. Ben has successfully handled hundreds of personal injury and automobile accident cases to the satisfaction of his clients.

Ben’s family law practice is wide and varied; from routine uncontested divorce cases to complex fault based divorces, equitable distribution of significant marital estates involving business and real property valuations, the pursuit and defense of spousal support, long, complex child custody issues involving parent relocation and third-party/grandparent custody/visitation matters. While separation and divorce are very stressful and uncertain times for the parties, Ben instills the guidance and confidence needed for his clients in such trying times.

Ben has also represented many clients who have suffered financial loss as a result of lawyers who have negligently represented their clients.

Ben is a member of the Virginia State Bar and Family Law Section, The Virginia Trial Lawyers Association and Family Law Section, The Fairfax County Bar Association and Family Law Section, a former member of the Fairfax County Bar Association Circuit Court Committee, and The Prince William County Bar Association and Family Law Section.

Ben has successfully handled hundreds of personal injury and automobile accident cases to the satisfaction of his clients.

Ben’s family law practice is wide and varied; from routine uncontested divorce cases to complex fault based divorces, equitable distribution of significant marital estates involving business and real property valuations, the pursuit and defense of spousal support, long, complex child custody issues involving parent relocation and third-party/grandparent custody/visitation matters. While separation and divorce are very stressful and uncertain times for the parties, Ben instills the guidance and confidence needed for his clients in such trying times.

Ben has also represented many clients who have suffered financial loss as a result of lawyers who have negligently represented their clients.

Ben is a member of the Virginia State Bar and Family Law Section, The Virginia Trial Lawyers Association and Family Law Section, The Fairfax County Bar Association and Family Law Section, a former member of the Fairfax County Bar Association Circuit Court Committee, and The Prince William County Bar Association and Family Law Section.

attorneys.name: William B. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Bill Smith has been engaged in the general practice of law for almost fifty years with a special emphasis on Civil Litigation in Courts of all levels in Virginia. The primary areas of law he has concentrated in are Personal Injury, Family Law, Employment Law, and Wills, Trusts and Administration of Estates.

The greater part of Bill Smith’s Civil Litigation Law Practice has been in representing the Plaintiff in the various legal areas mentioned above, although he has had several cases in which he represented the Defend/ant in such matters. He has prosecuted numerous jury and bench trials to conclusion in Virginia Circuit and Federal Courts and has handled appeals of cases in the Supreme Court of Virginia, the Court of Appeals of Virginia and the Federal U.S. Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Bill Smith believes strongly that the secret to the success of a trial lawyer is in the preparation of cases for trial to include accumulation of all the relevant facts, legal research of Virginia statutes and cases, (and other states as well when necessary), interviewing the client and witnesses and preparing them for trial and having ready exhibits for introduction into evidence at the trial. The strength of trial preparation in the great majority of cases leads to satisfactory settlement of the case.

Bill Smith’s practice also includes the mediation of virtually any type of legal controversy, particularly Family Law issues such as spousal support, child custody, visitation, child support and division of marital assets and his office practice includes office advice and preparation of wills and trusts. In mediation cases, Mr. Smith clearly explains the mediation process to the participants and calmly helps them work together to resolve all issues. His success in resolving controversies in mediation is equal to or in the excess of the national average of eighty-five percent (85%).

Awards and Honors

Honors

Winner of the American Bar Association Ross Essay Contest, 1976

Member of Virginia’s Legal Elite in Civil Litigation, 2003

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Richmond, VA
attorneys.bio:
William has dedicated his legal career to criminal defense. After serving in the United States Army, William joined the Chesterfield County Public Defender’s Office, where he was quickly promoted to Senior Trial Attorney.

During his tenure at the Public Defender’s Office, William tried the most cases of any attorney in the office. He has tried cases ranging from DUI to murder. If the case is important to the client, the case is important to him. William now represents clients throughout Virginia.

William’s goal for every case is to get the charges dropped, the client acquitted at trial, or the best outcome possible through a plea agreement. William is honest, hardworking and cares for people, no matter their circumstances.

Call him directly today to see what you both can do for your case. William also meets with clients face to face on weekday afternoons and weekends by appointment.

attorneys.name: Thomas G. Smith (Retired)
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Helping Clients in Virginia & Washington, D.C.

Tom Smith has focused his practice on medical malpractice cases involving serious injury or death for over thirty years. For seventeen years he defended doctors and hospitals on behalf of insurance companies, but since 1996 Tom's practice has been dedicated exclusively to representing patients and their families who have been injured or killed due to doctor or hospital errors. Tom has received many honors recognizing his skill and ability in trial litigation. He is an AV-rated lawyer by Martindale Hubbell, the highest rating by peers possible for professional and ethical standards.

Award-Winning Legal Counsel

Each year since 2006, Tom has been named as one of the Best Lawyers in America in the field of plaintiff's medical malpractice law. On three occasions in 2012, 2015, and most recently in 2019, Tom was named the Washington D.C. Metro Area Medical Malpractice Lawyer of the Year by Best Lawyers. He has also been named a Virginia and Metro D.C. Super Lawyer in the field of medical malpractice law every year since 2007. Only 5% of the lawyers in Virginia achieve the Super Lawyer status. Tom has also been named by both Washingtonian and Northern Virginia Magazine as a top lawyer in plaintiff's medical malpractice law. Finally, Tom has been named as a Top 100 Trial Lawyer by the American Trial Lawyers Association.

More important to Tom than these honors is the satisfaction he feels when he achieves a successful result for his client. Obviously, not every case is won, but all are fought with a dedication to the client.

attorneys.name: Austen Soare
attorneys.practice_type: Inmigration Lawyers in Salem, VA
attorneys.bio:
Austen is excited to be joining Amaryllis Law, where he will contribute to our team of dedicated legal advocates. Born and raised in Becker, Minnesota, Austen is the youngest of three brothers.

Austen’s passion for helping others has guided his career path. He has worked with several nonprofit organizations, including the Central Minnesota Mental Health Center and the Immigrant Law Center of Minnesota. Additionally, he served on the board of the Borromeo Legal Project, which provides pro bono legal services to individuals seeking U.S. citizenship. The principles Austen learned through these experiences continue to shape his approach to private practice.

Before joining Amaryllis Law, Austen worked as an immigration attorney at the Law Office of James Montana, where he handled a wide range of cases. He has represented clients in various immigration matters, including employment-based, family-based, and humanitarian cases. Austen also has significant courtroom experience, gained both at the Public Defender’s Office and as an immigration attorney advocating for individuals in removal proceedings.

Outside of work, Austen enjoys spending time with his family, exploring the outdoors, and indulging in a variety of cuisines. A passionate sports fan, he follows the Minnesota Timberwolves and Minnesota Vikings. Austen believes that the keys to a fulfilling life are laughter, joy, and finding meaning in every day.

attorneys.name: John M. Spencer
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Fredericksburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in New York City. At the age of 18 I joined the USAF and served during the 1st gulf war as a canine handler/ Law Enforcement Specialist 1988 - 1991. Upon my discharge I became a police officer in New York from 1992 - 1997. While a police officer I began to take college courses and moved to North Carolina to attend the University of North Carolina in 1997. I continued to work full time while attending and completing college as a police dispatcher. I received a Bachelors Degree in History with a 3.6 GPA and was awarded summa cum Laude. I was accepted into the University of North Carolina School of Law and graduated in 2003. After completion of my first year of law school I interned for the City of Charlotte or Mecklenburg County District Attorney's office where I prosecuted drug crimes. As this was not a paid position I also worked full time as a police dispatcher. After the second year of law school, I returned to the Charlotte, Mecklenburg County District Attorney's office and ran my own courtroom for the summer prosecuting all misdemeanor crimes. Again, this was not a paid position and I worked as a police Dispatcher full time to again support myself.

Upon completion of Law School in 2003, I moved to Virginia and worked at Steptoe & Johnson a large law firm in Washington DC in their International Trade section. once I passed the Virginia Bar Examination in 2003, I left this employment to focus on Criminal Law. Not having any contacts in Virginia I took a job at the Public Defenders's Office in Fredericksburg Virginia with the intention of it being a stepping stone to a prosecutor position. However, I fell in love with Criminal Defense work.

After one year in at the Public Defender's Office, I left to open my own law firm and have been in practice since that day.

As you can tell I was not born rich. I had to work full time while attending college full time. Once in law school I had to work twice as hard to support myself during the summer breaks. Working on full time job for free and another all night to eat. During my second and third years of law school I worked part-time at Belks department store to support myself. Put simply, I'm no stranger to hard work and I take that same approach with any case I handle. Every client has my cell phone and I even do Saturday appointments.

I have been practicing locally for over eleven years. You will find me in one of number of courts every day. I am a trial attorney who goes to court and tries cases everyday. I have tried everything from your average speeding ticket to 1st degree murder cases.

attorneys.name: Atchuthan "Sris" Sriskandarajah
attorneys.practice_type: Sex Crimes Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Atchuthan "Sris" Sriskandarajah is the owner and CEO of SRIS Law Group, P.C.

Mr. Sris started the firm in 1997 and today it is one of the few solely owned law firms that has client meeting locations in Virginia, Maryland and Chennai, India. The SRIS Law Group, P.C. has ten client meeting locations - seven in Virginia, two in Maryland and one in Chennai, India.

Mr. Sris was a former prosecutor for the Town of Haymarket, Virginia. As a result of his experience as a prosecutor in addition to being a very successful trial lawyer, his knowledge of criminal/traffic law and domestic relations is exemplary.

Attorneys who have been in practice for a greater period of time than Mr. Sris turn to him for advice on how to handle complex criminal and family law cases.

Mr. Sris has defended clients charged with criminal matters for over fifteen years. Some of the different types of criminal cases Mr. Sris has handled on behalf of his clients are armed robbery, malicious wounding, grand larceny, burglary, possession with intent to distribute marijuana, cocaine, heroin, etc. and sex offenses such as solicitation of a minor via the internet, rape, prostitution, child pornography, etc.

Mr. Sris will occasionally handle upon a special request traffic matters such as reckless driving, DUI or driving on a suspended license.

Due to Mr. Sris' experience as domestic relations litigator, he assists other attorneys in the firm with the more complex divorce cases, child custody matters, UCCJEA relocation cases.

If you wish to contact Mr. Sris, please contact him at the Fairfax Office. He can be reached at (703) 278-0405.

Kerry Stolz is an attorney focusing her practice on workers' compensation, insurance defense and civil litigation. Kerry routinely advises businesses by assessing the merits of workers' compensation and injury cases and the risks of defense of those cases. Kerry also works with business clients in general insurance defense matters and advises clients on the best defense practices for general liability claims. She is experienced in handling litigation disputes, including both full and final mediation and issue mediation.

REPRESENTATIVE CASES & TRANSACTIONS

Defended employer in an injured worker's appeal to the Full Commission on a claim for an open indemnity period. Successfully relied on an ineffective marketing defense at both the deputy commissioner level and the Full Commission which resulted in a significant indemnity savings to the employer.

Defended employer against claims for lifetime medicals, indemnity, and a permanency rating of a worker's amputated limb. Successful defense based on Claimant not proving an injury that occurred at a definite time with a sudden bodily change which saved the employer thousands of dollars in lifetime medical care.

Defended manufacturer against a workers' compensation claim filed for an injured worker's back injury claim. By relying on the defense that the worker lacked the required medical evidence for a back injury occurring on the date of accident, the employer achieved significant savings.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Szakaly
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Law Lawyers in Alexandria, VA
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Szakaly brings a distinctive interdisciplinary background in both law and health care to the firm. In addition to her legal practice, Jennifer is the owner and lead dentist of Isle of Wight Family and Cosmetic Dentistry, P.C., a role she has held since 2006. Her experience in the day-to-day clinical practice of dentistry provides her with invaluable insight into the dental anatomy, health care operations, current standards of practice, and other issues, strengthening her ability to represent injured patients in their professional negligence claims.

In 2023, Virginia Governor Glenn Youngkin appointed Jennifer to Virginia’s Board of Dentistry. She was confirmed by the Virginia Senate during the following legislative session. As a member of the Board of Dentistry, Jennifer has worked to set standards for the conduct of Virginia dentists, to ensure that competent dental care is being provided to Virginia’s dental patients, and to analyze and impose disciplinary action when appropriate standards are not being followed.

Jennifer is also an experienced educator. She has served as an Adjunct Clinical Professor at the Medical College of Virginia School of Dentistry, mentoring dental students in clinical settings and contributing to curriculum development. Her commitment to service has also been reflected in her long tenure on the Board of Directors for Court Appointed Special Advocates (CASA), where she served from 2009 to 2025.

Jennifer earned her Juris Doctor from Regent University School of Law and her Doctor of Dental Surgery from Virginia Commonwealth University. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Biology and English from The College of William and Mary.

attorneys.name: Kerri Borchardt Taylor
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Charlottesville, VA
attorneys.bio: Mrs. Taylor is a lifelong resident of Charlottesville. She received a basketball scholarship to James Madison University, where she obtained both her undergraduate and MBA degrees. In 1995, Mrs. Taylor graduated from The University of Richmond, The T.C. Williams School of Law, where she was a member of Law Review. Mrs. Taylor began her legal career in 1995 with McGuire Woods, LLP, one of the largest law firms in the United States. There she worked as an associate gaining valuable litigation and trial experience while assisting in the representation of a variety of clients including VMI and Fortune 500 companies such as Westinghouse, Steele, Ford, Philip Morris, Cincinnati Insurance, ConAgra and Pepsi. Mrs. Taylor continued her litigation career as a Senior Associate with Morin & Barkley, LLP, where she successfully resolved a traumatic brain injury case involving UM/UIM coverage issues resulting in a $1.25 million dollar settlement for the client. She spent 9 years as a Partner with Goodman, Allen & Filetti, PLLC, where she focused her practice on personal injury, family law, nursing home and medical malpractice, workers’ compensation, commercial disputes and trust and estate litigation. In January 2014, Mr. Hart and Mrs. Taylor formed Hart Taylor. The firm blends their civil and criminal expertise and allows them to offer clients throughout Central Virginia a combined 40 years of litigation experience. Mrs. Taylor has attained the "BV" Distinguished rating through The Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings ™. This is an objective assessment of a lawyer's high ethical standards and professional ability based on ratings and evaluations performed by judges and other lawyers. Mrs. Taylor is a past member of the Charlottesville-Albemarle Bar Association's Board of Directors, a member of the Virginia State Bar, Virginia State Bar Family Law Section, Charlottesville-Albemarle Bar Association, and Charlottesville-Albemarle Bar Association's Family Law Section, Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, and Virginia Trial Lawyers Association's Family Law Section. Mrs. Taylor is admitted to practice in Virginia and before the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Virginia, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, and the 4th Circuit Court of Appeals.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fairfax, VA
attorneys.bio:
K. Leigh Taylor received a B.A. in Government and Spanish from the College of William and Mary and her J.D. from George Mason University School of Law.

After receiving her law degree, Leigh was the recipient of a Clinical Teaching Fellowship at the Domestic Violence Institute at Northeastern University School of Law in Boston, Massachusetts. Through the fellowship, she taught law students to advocate for victims of domestic violence in two separate legal clinics. After her return from Boston, Leigh joined the firm and is now a shareholder.

Leigh is an active member of the Virginia State Bar, Fairfax Bar Association, Virginia Bar Association, Virginia Trial Lawyers Association, Arlington Bar Association, and the Virginia Women Attorneys Association. Leigh is a Director on the Fairfax Bar Association Board of Directors and past chair of the Circuit Court Committee and Pro Bono Committee. She also is a member of the Public Service Committee of the Virginia Bar Association and a member of the Rule 6.1 Society of Legal Services of Northern Virginia.

Leigh has practiced exclusively domestic relations law since 2003, in Fairfax County, the City of Alexandria, and the counties of Arlington, Loudoun, and Prince William. She represents clients and their interests through negotiation, mediation, and litigation.

Joe is a partner at von Keller Thelin Williams, PC where his practice focuses on Estate Planning, Estate Administration (Probate), Trust Administration, Estate and Trust Litigation, and Guardianship and Conservatorship. He is committed to helping clients safeguard their legacy. He regularly appears in the Courts of Prince William, Fairfax, and Loudoun Counties. Joe can help with:

Preparing Estate Plans, including Wills and Trusts

Creating Powers of Attorney

Creating Advance Medical Directives

Establishing Guardianship and Conservatorship

Assisting Executors, Administrators, and other Personal Representatives with the administration of estates

Will contests or other estate and fiduciary litigation.

Joe is an Eagle Scout (for real). He is a graduate of the University of Tennessee and a dedicated Vols fan. He lives in Fairfax County with his wife, two young daughters and the family dogs, Cisco and Grimm.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Steven D. Barnette, P.C
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Hampton, VA
attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Southwest Virginia where I graduated from high school at the top of the class, well 2nd anyway, and was the second person in my family to attend college. I was fortunate enough to attend The College of William & Mary. Those years in The College were so filled with history and inspiration from our founding fathers that I was motivated to pursue law as a career. Also during my college years, I worked as a cook in a local candy and confectionary store for which I still have very fond memories of and I feel it has been a major addition to my life. I mean, how many people can say they can write a doctore level thesis and make five different flavors of fudge at the same time. I graduated from The College in 1998 with my BBA in Accounting and after graduating from William & Mary, I went to law school at Regent University. attorneys.name: E. Diane Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Taxation Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Diane Thompson is a firm shareholder and leader of the firm's wills, trusts, estate planning and administration practice group. She is nationally recognized for her legal practice focusing on estate and wealth transfer planning, trusts and estates administration, and taxation.

A highly respected estate and tax planning lawyer, Diane is a much sought after advisor to ultra high and high net worth individuals and families on the broad range of very complex estate planning concerns. She focuses on personalized planning with an emphasis on reducing the tax impact of federal income, estate, gift and generation-skipping transfer taxes to maximize the transfer of wealth. She guides personal representatives through the estate administration process and prepares estate tax returns, inheritance tax returns and fiduciary income tax returns of the United States and other jurisdictions.

One focus of Diane's practice is post-mortem tax and disclaimer planning. She maintains the most complete compilation of estate and tax reference resources in the country on disclaimer law, which is used nationally by many other professionals.

Diane is a frequent lecturer, particularly on the subject "Disclaimers: When, Why & How to Say ‘No' to an Inheritance." She has lectured at many top industry conferences including the University of Miami Heckerling Institute on Estate Planning, Notre Dame Tax and Estate Planning Conference, Duke Estate Planning Conference, Southern California Tax & Estate Planning Forum, among others.

Diane authored "Chap. 13, When it is Better to Disclaim Than to Receive: Proceedings of the 39th Annual Heckerling Institute on Estate Planning" (Matthew Bender & Co. 2005). Additionally, she has instructed courses for numerous state CPA societies.

From 1988 through 1996, Diane taught courses in advanced estate planning and federal taxation of estates, gifts and trusts at William & Mary Law School.

REPRESENTATIVE CASES & TRANSACTIONS

Structured a plan of numerous disclaimers, to include the use of the credit for tax on prior transfers, for husband and wife estates with combined assets of $7,500,000 resulting in an estate tax savings of $1,700,000.

Prepared an estate plan using grantor retained annuity trusts, and other irrevocable trusts, resulting in millions of dollars saved in transfer taxes.

Prepared an estate plan which included provisions for the transfer of Roth IRAs, via trusts, to grandchildren which will result in income tax free growth for a long period of time for the grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Christopher J. Toepp
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fredericksburg, VA
attorneys.bio:
Chris dedicates his practice to helping clients and making his community a safer place. He has earned a reputation as an exceptional litigator in the courtroom. With nearly a decade of trial experience, he has handled hundreds of bench and jury trials in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Chris knows how to present evidence so that the jury comprehends his client's hardships and the impact their injuries have had on their lives.

Chris is a shareholder at the Allen & Allen law firm, and works on a wide range of personal injury cases including car crashes, truck accidents and motorcycle wrecks. Injured in a tractor-trailer accident in 2007, Chris has a first-hand understanding of what personal injury clients go through in the aftermath of an accident including the physical pain, the impact on loved ones, and the financial burdens incurred along the road to recovery. He strives to guide and protect those experiencing these difficult situations so that they may concentrate fully on their healing.

Chris graduated from Dartmouth College in 2004, where he was part of the Division I Swim and Dive team. He then received his law degree from the William and Mary School of Law. Before joining Allen & Allen, he served as an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney in Richmond, prosecuting a variety of cases including murder, robbery, animal cruelty, DUI, and hit and run. He believes in the effectiveness of the judicial process and enjoys being in the courtroom.

Chris is an avid golfer and enjoys fishing, boating, and watching his daughter's swim meets. He lives in Richmond.

attorneys.name: Amy E. Totten
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Warrenton, VA
attorneys.bio:
Amy E. Totten always puts herself in the shoes of her opponent. As a former prosecutor, she knows the importance of being prepared for trial and seeing all sides of a case, especially when her clients are dealing with difficult life-altering events.

During her two decades of legal practice, Amy has handled thousands of cases from traffic cases and simple support matters to intricate divorce cases, child sexual assault crimes and capital murder cases. She draws on this wealth of experience for every legal issue that she tackles. Because of her years of work as a prosecutor, Amy honed her investigative skills using every tool available to build her case. She implemented and oversaw the special grand jury system in Loudoun County, allowing prosecutors to thoroughly examine challenging evidence/witnesses and revive unsolved cold cases. Amy uses that investigative experience to develop a powerful case and strategy in complex asset divorces, challenging child custody disputes and contested domestic relations matters. Amy’s background has also helped her to recognize when it is in a client’s best interest to collaborate with specialists such as business evaluators, forensic accountants, and health professionals.

Though Amy is often able to get her clients the outcome they desire in the courtroom, she is also a veteran negotiator. She understands the complexity of her client’s cases from both a legal perspective, and on an emotional level. She helps clients balance their own interests—relationships with their children, financial stability and the costs of litigation. When settlement is a client’s goal, Amy utilizes various tools such as property settlement agreements, mediation, and conferences with opposing counsel to negotiate a positive resolution for her client. attorneys.name: William D Tucker III
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Charlottesville, VA
attorneys.bio:
Charlottesville attorney William D. Tucker, III is the founding partner of Tucker Griffin Barnes P.C., and one of Charlottesville’s leading experts in real estate law. Mr. Tucker’s 45 plus years of experience as a real estate lawyer, and his business acumen have helped create the success of Tucker Griffin Barnes. He also is co-founder of Charlottesville Settlement Company, Central Virginia’s largest settlement and title insurance company. People seek out “Tucker” (as he likes to be called) for his real estate and business expertise.

Tucker received his undergraduate degree in Business Administration from the University of Florida and then earned his Doctor of Jurisprudence (JD) from the University of Virginia. He was subsequently admitted to the bar in both Virginia and Florida.

Tucker resides in Charlottesville with Elly, his wife of 35 years. Their daughter, Dory, is a former elementary school teacher in Richmond, and their son, Josh, is a 4th year student at the University of Richmond. Tucker’s eldest son, Tee, is a realtor in the Charlottesville area. Tucker is also grandfather to Liam Tucker, and twins, Audrey and David Doyle.

Tucker is an active member in the community – literally. Every Sunday he perfects his jump shot with a group of aging basketball players. Tucker is also an avid supporter of the local performing arts and is a dedicated member of Congregation Beth Israel and a board member of Camp Albemarle Inc. Tucker also has served as a board member of the Piedmont Housing Alliance, Tandem Friends School, Virginia Institute of Autism, First Night Virginia, and for 15 years, was a faithful and active member, and provided legal assistance to the Board that refurbished and reopened The Paramount Theater.

High client return rate:

Tucker and his real estate staff are dedicated to treating every client with professionalism and courtesy. The impact of this approach has resulted in a significant percentage of clients returning for future transactions or referring their friends and family to Tucker and his team. Tucker wants to earn and keep your business.

Tucker’s basic advice to anyone buying or selling real estate:

For buyers:

Select an experienced real estate agent and settlement attorney early in the process.

Shop for Homeowner’s insurance and include your car in the pricing, as some discounts may be available.

Understand that the actual amount of cash needed to close may not be known until just before closing (sometimes not until the day of closing.)

For sellers:

Select an experienced real estate agent who has knowledge of your local market.

Provide a copy of the title insurance policy and physical survey to your listing agent.

Leave the utilities on until the actual settlement and transfer of title.

Tucker’s Tips:

Every week, Tucker publishes “Tucker’s Tips” — advice for local Realtors and Lenders. These tips cover topics from dealing with homeowner’s association dues to selling distressed properties. In fact, Tucker is locally known as a distressed property expert. He has established a team of paralegals who deal entirely with short sales. Tucker and his short sale paralegals offer legal advice to involved parties, negotiate with lenders, and handle the closings for what can often be a stressful situation.

What some of his clients have said:

“Mr. Tucker, I cannot thank you enough for all your work. I wish everyone had your work ethic and attention to detail and level of customer service. This would never have gone through had you not been on the case. We thank you from the bottom of our hearts.”

“Bill Tucker and his team were the answer to my real estate prayers! After being transferred to another state for work, my condo sat on the market for over a year in this dismal market with no traffic. I enlisted the help of Bill Tucker and after 3 months, I was relieved of this burden! They fought hard so that I wouldn’t have to continue to pay on my condo even after the short sale was over. I truly felt that they cared about me and my situation and could not have asked for a better team. THANK you!”

“I just wanted to express my gratitude to Christen Pugh, Valerie Johnson, Bill Tucker and all who work so hard to make dealing with short sales and real estate transactions easier! Thanks is too small a word.”

“I just want to say thank you for your help. You were extremely helpful. Your experience and knowledge were valuable and reassuring. I want to share that Valerie and Debbie were rock stars. They were organized and professional with just the right amount of push to get us to get them what they needed. Honestly, this went about as good as Ali and I could have hoped in terms of both the transaction coming to fruition but also in terms of the service Valerie and Debbie provided.”

attorneys.name: Russell W. Updike
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Covington, VA
attorneys.bio:
Russell W. "Russ" Updike came to Covington, Virginia from Richmond in 1990. He received his B.S. degree from Virginia Commonwealth University in 1986 and his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Richmond T. C. Williams School of Law in 1990. Mr. Updike joined the firm of William T. Wilson and Associates in 1990 and engaged in the general practice of law until becoming a partner in the firm of Wilson & Updike in 1994. For the past 25 years Mr. Updike has practiced almost exclusively injury law representing individuals in personal injury, medical malpractice and workers' compensation claims. During the past 25 years, Mr. Updike has had the pleasure of being lead counsel in several jury trials resulting in verdicts of $1,000,000 or more for his clients, including a verdict in 2012 in the amount of $2,644,373 (inclusive of interest), which is the largest verdict returned by a jury in the history of Alleghany County.

Mr. Updike is a member of the Virginia Trial Lawyers Association (VTLA). He has served as a representative of the VTLA Board of Governors from 1998 until 2008. He has also been active with the Virginia State Bar, serving as a member of the Eighth District Committee from 1998 to 2004 before being appointed to the Virginia State Bar Disciplinary Board on July 1, 2004, where he served until July 2010. Mr. Updike also served as a representative of the Young Lawyers Conference of the Virginia State Bar from 1994 to 1996. He also served multiple terms as President of the Alleghany-Bath-Highland Bar Association. Currently, Mr. Updike has been listed in the Virginia Super Lawyer Magazine for approximately 10 years. Mr. Updike is also a member of the Virginia Law Foundation Fellows, Class of 2009.

Mr. Updike has been involved in the community by serving on the boards of the Salvation Army, Jackson River Enterprises and the Alleghany Highlands Chamber of Commerce. Mr. Updike has been chairman of the Board of Directors for Jackson River Enterprises since 2010.

Mr. Updike is married to the former Jennifer Lilly of Lewisburg, West Virginia and they have twin boys, Eli Jackson and Trent Justice, who were born in March of 2004 as well as Ava Grace who was born in July of 2010.

attorneys.name: Hugo Raul Valverde
attorneys.practice_type: International Transactions Lawyers in Virginia Beach, VA
attorneys.bio:
Hugo graduated with honors from Regent University School of Law in Virginia Beach, where he served as a senior editor of the Regent University Law Review. Prior to attending law school, he earned a master's degree in environmental management from Duke University and a Bachelor of Science degree from the College of William and Mary. Hugo has published articles in the Journal of Coastal Research and the Journal of Coastal Management. Hugo is a member of the Virginia State Bar, the Hispanic National Bar Association, the American Immigration Lawyers Association, and a Board Member of the Hampton Roads Hispanic Chamber of Commerce. In the past, he served as co-chair of the Immigrant Outreach Committee of the Virginia State Bar Young Lawyers Conference and a legal advisor to the Illegal Immigration and Crimes Task Force of the Virginia Crimes Commission. Hugo teaches immigration law at Regent University School of Law in Virginia Beach, Virginia.

He is also admitted to practice as a registered patent attorney before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

Hugo's passion for immigration law stems from his own family's immigration experience. His father and mother came to the United States from Peru fleeing political persecution, and as he grew up, Hugo spent many summers in Peru. Hugo uses his experience growing up in an immigrant family and time abroad to understand the conditions where his clients or their employees may have come from and the challenges they face when they come to the United States. He uses this understanding to provide better service to his clients.

Prior to starting Valverde & Rowell, Hugo served as an attorney advisor to the Immigration Courts in Oakdale and New Orleans, Louisiana, and Memphis, Tennessee. The U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review selected him for this position under the highly competitive U.S. Attorney General's Honors Program. As a law student, he volunteered with the local office of the Diocese of Richmond's Catholic Refugee and Immigration Services.

Before attending law school, Hugo worked for several years as an environmental planner with the Hampton Roads Planning District Commission. At the Commission, he represented local governments on state advisory committees, analyzed the impact of proposed federal and state regulations on local governments, and assisted the local governments of Hampton Roads develop municipal and construction stormwater runoff programs and Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act programs that complied with federal and state environmental laws.

After growing up in the Washington, D.C., area, since 1990 Hugo has spent most of his life in the Hampton Roads, Virginia, area. He is proud to call Virginia Beach home where he enjoys spending time with his wife and five children and surfing.

In 2008, Hugo received the R. Edwin Burnette Jr. Young Lawyer of the Year Award from the Virginia State Bar Young Lawyers Conference.

His father and mother came to the United States from Peru fleeing political persecution, and as he grew up, Hugo spent many summers in Peru. Hugo uses his experience growing up in an immigrant family and time abroad to understand the conditions where his clients or their employees may have come from and the challenges they face when they come to the United States. He uses this understanding to provide better service to his clients.

Prior to starting Valverde & Rowell, Hugo served as an attorney advisor to the Immigration Courts in Oakdale and New Orleans, Louisiana, and Memphis, Tennessee. The U.S. Department of Justice, Executive Office for Immigration Review selected him for this position under the highly competitive U.S. Attorney General's Honors Program. As a law student, he volunteered with the local office of the Diocese of Richmond's Catholic Refugee and Immigration Services.

Before attending law school, Hugo worked for several years as an environmental planner with the Hampton Roads Planning District Commission. At the Commission, he represented local governments on state advisory committees, analyzed the impact of proposed federal and state regulations on local governments, and assisted the local governments of Hampton Roads develop municipal and construction stormwater runoff programs and Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act programs that complied with federal and state environmental laws.

After growing up in the Washington, D.C., area, since 1990 Hugo has spent most of his life in the Hampton Roads, Virginia, area. He is proud to call Virginia Beach home where he enjoys spending time with his wife and five children and surfing.

In 2008, Hugo received the R. Edwin Burnette Jr. Young Lawyer of the Year Award from the Virginia State Bar Young Lawyers Conference.

attorneys.bio:
With over a decade of experience, Maggy R. Vaughn has developed significant expertise in complex family legal matters, focusing particularly on adoption law. Ms. Vaughn is a member of the American Academy of Adoption and Assisted Reproduction Attorneys, an organization of elite adoption attorneys who have demonstrated the highest level of competence and ethical standards. Ms. Vaughn also serves as a Guardian ad litem (GAL) providing her a unique perspective on complex family law matters and issues.

CAPTURING THE ESSENCE OF A CLIENT, ONE STORY AT A TIME

Her representative matters include agency adoption, direct parental placement, step-parent adoptions, close relative adoptions, adoption option consultations, third party custody matters, and foster parent representation. Ms. Vaughn also handles child custody, divorce, child support, visitation, paternity and other family law matters. Ms. Vaughn's practice is characterized by a comprehensive approach offering clients expert guidance through sensitive legal matters.

NO FALSE PROMISES, ONLY HARD WORK

There are no guarantees of an outcome when it comes to your legal problems. (If only that were not true!) But there is a way to put your best foot forward. Through dedicated representation and continual contact, you can rest assured knowing Ms. Vaughn is asserting her best efforts to support you. You will have an advocate who will fight hard for you against a complicated and often unforgiving system.

attorneys.name: William L. Waller
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Falls Church, VA
attorneys.bio:
William Waller (Billy) is an associate attorney at Maddox & Gerock. Since joining the firm, Billy has worked on a variety of family law cases, particularly custody and visitation, child and spousal support, and equitable distribution. Whether advocating in court, drafting marital settlement agreements, or preparing discovery, Billy works enthusiastically on every assignment in order to deliver the best results to Maddox & Gerock’s clients.

Prior to joining Maddox & Gerock, Billy was a Judicial Law Clerk for the Seventh Judicial Circuit of Virginia in Newport News. While clerking, Billy worked predominately on family law matters. Recognizing the emotional difficulties and personal stakes implicated in all family law cases, Billy is committed to working zealously for his clients as they navigate through life’s most challenging transitions.

Billy obtained his Juris Doctor from William & Mary Law School and is licensed to practice law in Virginia. During law school, Billy served as the Editor-in-Chief of the William & Mary Bill of Rights Journal, a Teaching Assistant for the 1L Legal Practice Program, and a Board Member of the Public Service Fund. He was also awarded the CALI Excellence for the Future Award for receiving the highest grade in Legal Practice I as well as a Dean’s Certificate at graduation for outstanding service and contributions to the law school community.

Billy received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Virginia, earning a double major in Foreign Affairs and Sociology. He subsequently worked in the philanthropic non-profit sector for several years before returning to law school to pursue his lifelong career goal of becoming a family law lawyer.

Born and raised in Arlington, Billy is proud to advocate for and represent clients from his hometown and the greater Northern Virginia region. In his free time, Billy enjoys traveling, going to the movies, and swimming. He also loves spending quality time with his niece and nephew.
